SUBJECT: Merging of Radio Stations

With reference to the attached extract of an article under the heading "Five Radio Stations will Be Merged" appearing in the March 31st issue of the "Shanghai Times", the undersigned interviewed Mr. Tai, a clerk of the Shanghai Broadcasting Station on March 3 and ascertained the following :-

The Greater Shanghai Broadcasting Station and other broadcasting stations in Nanking, Hankow, Soochow, and Hangchow which had been controlled by the Japanese military, together with the Daito (Great Eastern) Broadcasting Station located at No. 340 Yantzepoo Road which had been managed by the Japanese Foreign Office, were placed under the control of the newly organized Chinese Broadcasting Enterprise Construction Association (中國廣播事業建設協會) at Nanking on February 22, 1941. This association is an organ jointly established by a Japanese-Chinese corporation.

主题：广播电台合并

鉴于附上的《上海泰晤士报》3月31日刊中题为“五家广播电台将合并”的文章摘录，具名者于3月3日会见了上海广播电台职员戴先生（Mr. Tai），并查明以下情况：

大上海广播电台以及南京、汉口、苏州和杭州等地此前由日军控制的广播电台，连同位于杨树浦路340号、由日本外务省管理的大东广播电台，于1941年2月22日置于新成立于南京的中国广播事业建设协会的控制之下。该协会是由中日合办机构共同建立的机关。

大东（XQHA）广播电台和大上海广播电台实际上已于3月26日合并为上海广播电台（XGOS）。该广播电台将负责对华及对国外的广播业务，而大东广播电台将保留其名称，使用呼号“XQHA”，主要面向当地日本居民进行广播。

Broadcasting stations in Nanking,

Soochow will be merged shortly to

stated.
A dinner party will be given on
April 6 with the attendance of Mr.

of the Nanking Government, an-

Shanghai Broadcasting Station, it
was learnt.

April 3, 1941.

Merging of Radio Stations

With reference to the attached extract of an
article under the heading "Five Radio Stations will Be
"Merged" appearing in the March 31st issue of the "Shanghai
Times", the undersigned interviewed Mr. Ni, a clerk of
the Shanghai Broadcasting Station on March 3 and ascer-
tained the following :-

The Greater Shanghai Broadcasting Station and
other broadcasting stations in Nanking, Hankow, Soochow,
and Hangchow which had been controlled by the Japanese
military, together with the Daito (Great Eastern)
Broadcasting Station located at No. 340 Yantzepoo Road
which had been managed by the Japanese Foreign Office,
were placed under the control of the newly organized
Chinese Broadcasting Enterprise Construction Association
(中國廣播事業建設協會) at Nanking on February 22,
1941. This association is an organ jointly established
by a Japanese-Chinese corporation.

The Great Eastern (XQHA) Broadcasting Station
and the Greater Shanghai Broadcasting Station were
actually merged into the Shanghai Broadcasting Station
(XGO) on March 26. This Broadcasting Station will
handle broadcasting directed towards China and foreign
countries, while the Great Eastern Broadcasting Station
will retain its name, use its call-sign "XQHA" and carry
out broadcasting mainly to local Japanese residents.

On March 26, all the staff formerly in the employ
of the Great Eastern Broadcasting Station removed to the
second floor of the Astor House, where the offices of
the Shanghai Broadcasting Station are located; thus,
they are now attached to the Shanghai Broadcasting

广播电台合并

鉴于附上的《上海泰晤士报》3月31日刊中题为“五家广播电台将合并”的文章摘录，具名者于3月3日会见了上海广播电台职员倪先生（Mr. Ni），并查明以下情况：

大上海广播电台以及南京、汉口、苏州和杭州等地此前由日军控制的广播电台，连同位于杨树浦路340号、由日本外务省管理的大东广播电台，于1941年2月22日置于新成立于南京的中国广播事业建设协会的控制之下。该协会是由中日合办机构共同建立的机关。

大东（XQHA）广播电台和大上海广播电台实际上已于3月26日合并为上海广播电台（XGO）。该广播电台将负责对华及对国外的广播业务，而大东广播电台将保留其名称，使用呼号“XQHA”，主要面向当地日本居民进行广播。

3月26日，原受雇于大东广播电台的所有职员迁至礼查饭店二楼，即上海广播电台办事处所在地；因此，他们现在隶属于上海广播

SUBJECT:
According to the regulations governing the
formation of the organization, the Corporation will
undertake work :
(a) pertaining to construction of broadcasting enterprises
(b) pertaining to unified operation of radio broadcasting
station,
(c) pertaining to collection, safekeeping and distribu-
tion of funds for constructional purposes in broad-
casting enterprises,
(d) pertaining to establishment of relations with
broadcasting enterprises in foreign countries, and
(e) to carry out work specially required by the Govern-
ment, in connection with broadcasting enterprises.
An agreement is stated to have been signed
between the Nanking Government and the Japanese authori-
ties regarding the handing over of control of Japanese
sponsored broadcasting stations in Shanghai, Hankow,
Nanking, Soochow and Hangchow.
However, according to information obtained from
people connected with the local broadcasting circles,
the Japanese have agreed to hand over the control of all
broadcasting stations in places in Central China other
than those in Shanghai. Negotiations concerning the
handing over of Japanese sponsored radio stations in
Shanghai, it is reported, are still in progress, and so
far, no attempt has been made by the Corporation to
seize the control of private commercial stations here,
which still lies with the Japanese Broadcasting Superin-
tendent's Office, Hardoon Building, Nanking Road.

Made by... D.S.I. MacAdie Forwarded by...

The Wha Shing Broadcasting Station, 25 Chihli
Road, was ordered to suspend broadcasting from November
13, 1939 by the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendent's
Office, Harpoon Building, Nanking Road. This order
was issued because the Wha Shing Station jointly
broadcast with the Wha Tung Station, 365 Kwangse Road,
a special programme for the Seen You Zoo Company
(三友實業社), 387 Nanking Road, on November 12, 13 and
14, and was therefore considered to have violated the
regulations governing registration by co-operating with
a non-registered radio station. The Wha Tung Station
is British owned and not registered with the Japanese,
the broadcasting hours of the station being chiefly
taken up by the Seen You Zoo Company.

A special broadcasting programme, sponsored by
the Shanghai Entertainers' Lien Yi Society, 44 Yunnan
Road, on behalf of a number of shows, which was
scheduled to be broadcast from the Dah Yah Station,
94 Hinkiang Road and the Sing Sang Broadcasting Station,
423 Nanking Road, on November 16, was prohibited by
the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendent's Office.
The Shanghai Entertainers' Lien Yi Society had not
applied to the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendent's
Office for permission to hold this broadcast and is
not registered with that office.

The Broadcasting Superintendent's Office has
now issued instructions to various radio stations that

pages.en:
Thereupon, with a view to giving them another and the
last chance for reconsidering themselves, we ordered them to
attend this office so as to caution them in a most lenient
manner, but they failed to do so.
In the light of these circumstances, the above-mentioned
two broadcasting stations could not but be regarded as having
abandoned the right of operating as authorized radio broad-
casting stations.
While we were contemplating to forcibly shut down the
two stations, they published advertisements in newspapers to
the effect that the ownership of the stations was transferred
to Charles Madar & Co., (British), in the early part of De-
cember, 1938, for the purpose of escaping forcible measures
which would have been taken by this office.
Broadcasting is the work to be permitted only to spe-
cific persons by a Government and not to be undertaken by
any person freely. Therefore, the act of buying and selling
between private individuals can not, as a matter of course,
be regarded as valid.
We do not recognize the above-mentioned broadcasting
stations as British owned, although they are functioning
under the name of a British subject.
We have the right to close the said stations, because we
still regard them as being managed by the Chinese, but think-
ing it advisable to approach the British Consul-General to
close them down in order to avoid unnecessary friction, we
have been negotiating with the British Consul-General since
the last Summer. A letter dated February 12, 1940 has been
received from the Consul-General stating that the two sta-
tions in question, having been sold to Miss. L. Milanowska,
a Polish citizen, and that Mr. Madar's interest in those concerns
ceased as from February 1, 1940. (Vide the attached letter)
pages.zh:
随后，为了给它们最后一次重新考虑的机会，我们命令它们前来本办公室，以便以最宽容的方式对它们提出警告，但它们并未照办。
鉴于上述情况，上述两家广播电台只能被视为已放弃作为授权广播电台的经营权。
就在我们考虑强制关闭这两家电台时，它们在报纸上刊登广告，声称电台所有权已于1938年12月初转让给查尔斯·马达尔公司（Charles Madar & Co.，英商），旨在逃避本办公室将采取的强制措施。
广播是政府仅允许特定人员从事的工作，而非任何人可自由进行的事业。因此，私人之间的买卖行为当然不能被视为有效。
尽管上述广播电台以英国臣民的名义运作，但我们不承认其为英商所有。
我们有权关闭上述电台，因为我们仍视其由华人管理，但认为为避免不必要的摩擦，通过英国总领事馆将其关闭更为妥当，因此自去年夏季以来一直与英国总领事馆进行交涉。已收到1940年2月12日总领事来函，称涉案两家电台已出售给波兰公民 L. Milanowska 小姐，且马达尔先生在这些企业中的权益自1940年2月1日起终止。（见附件信函）

As the Poles do not enjoy the extraterritorial rights in
China, the stations in question, therefore, are under the con-
trol of your authorities.
In view of the above, we should be much obliged if you
would cause steps to be taken for the immediate closing of the
two radio broadcasting stations.
Yours faithfully,
(Sealed) K. Asano,
Chief of the Radio
Broadcasting Control Office.

鉴于上述情况，如蒙贵方采取步骤立即关闭这两家广播电台，我们将不胜感激。

REPORT
File No.
Date January 25, 1940

Subject. Registration of Radio Stations and Entertainers by the Japanese
Broadcasting Superintendent's Office.

Made by D. S. I. MacAdie Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

With reference to the attached translation of
extract from the Sin Shun Pao (Japanese owned Chinese
language newspaper) dated January 23, 1940, regarding
the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendent's Office
ordering radio stations and persons engaged in broadcasts
to register, all broadcasting stations in the
International Settlement and French Concession, with
the exception of a few foreign owned, have now
registered with the Superintendent's Office since the
inauguration of the Superintendent's Office in 1938.
The registration permits are valid for one year from
the date of issue and required to be renewed on
expiration.

In June, 1939, the Broadcasting Superintendent's
Office conducted a registration of entertainers engaged
in broadcasts at various stations and registration
certificates were issued. These certificates were to
expire on December 31, 1939, and consequently in the
beginning of January, 1940, the Superintendent's Office
issued a circular order notifying the entertainers to
renew their registration and pay a registration fee of
$2. Later another order was issued stating that
entertainers failing to register would be prohibited
from broadcasting and that the Superintendent's Office
would detail representatives to investigate the matter.
So far, no representatives of the office have visited
the radio stations concerning the registration of
entertainers.

(Vice Special Br.
report dated
30.6.39)

A.C. (Sp. Br.)
D. S. I.

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper) :-
ATTEMPT TO ENFORCE REGISTRATION OF RADIO STATIONS

On New Year's Day the Shanghai Radio Broadcasting
Stations' Supervision Office issued a notice to all radio
broadcasting stations in Shanghai ordering them as well as
those who are engaged to make broadcasts to apply to the
Office for registration and to enclose $2 each as a fee.
The registration had to be effected before January 18.
Yesterday the Office notified all radio
broadcasting stations to the effect that any station which
had failed to register should cease operations at once.
In the meantime the Office has detailed men to make
investigations as to whether these broadcasting stations
have applied for registration. It is said that drastic
measures will be taken to deal with any station which had
failed to comply with this order.

June 30, 1939.

Japanese Radio Broadcasting Control Office - registers
broadcasting entertainers.

Local radio broadcasting stations, which are registered
with the Japanese Radio Broadcasting Control Office, Hardoon
Building, Nanking Road, have received notifications from
the Control Office ordering broadcasting entertainers to
register.

The first notification which was dated June 10, request-
ed the station managements to notify the entertainers engaged
in broadcasting at the respective stations to register with
the Radio Broadcasting Control Office before June 20, 1939.
The other, dated June 20, stated that the period for regis-
tration had expired and that many entertainers had complied
with the order and were granted registration certificates.
This notice requested the station managements to prevent
all entertainers, who are not registered, from broadcasting
with effect from July 1, 1939.

According to the registration certificate, the enter-
tainer should observe the following:-

1. Obey the rules and regulations of the Radio Broad-
casting Control Office.
2. Not to engage in reactionary activities or broadcast
programmes of a reactionary nature.
3. Not to broadcast programmes from stations which are
not registered.

The certificates will be valid until December 31, 1939.

Certified true copy

JHS.

Subject Letter from Major Asano on subject of dispute between the

(XHHV) on the question of wavelength K.C.780.

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford.

With reference to the attached letter, dated
10.12.38 addressed to the Police Department, S.M.C.,
by Major Asano on the subject of the dispute which has
arisen between the American Commercial Broadcasting
Station (XMHE ) owned by Mr. P.H. Vanmeter (American) and
the Yeu Lien Broadcasting Station (XHHV) on the question of the
adoption of the same carrier frequency wavelength, i.e. K.C.
780, full details of the manner in which the dispute arose
are on record in attached Special Branch reports under the
respective headings of the two stations in question.

Briefly stated, the position is as follows :-
Mr. Vanmeter addressed a letter to the Special Branch, dated
11.11.38, announcing that he had established a broadcasting
station (XMHE) K.C. 780 at Lane 97, House 36 , Myburgh Road.
Enquiries revealed that Mr. Vanmeter's ownership of the
station was duly registered with the American Consulate-
General. At the time Mr. Vanmeter's station was established,
no intimation had been received from either the Broadcasting
Superintendence Office or from the Yeu Lien Station (XHHV)
of its intention to commence broadcasting. It should be
mentioned, however, that on 3.10.38, the Yeu Lien Station,
which had suspended broadcasting in April, 1938, applied
for permission to reopen the station. The management of
the Yeu Lien station was informed, in accordance with the
agreement arrived at between the Police and the Japanese,
that before the application could be granted, it would be
necessary to obtain the permission of the Japanese but the
Yeu Lien station refused to approach the Japanese and the

主题 浅野少校关于美国商业电台 (XMHE) 与友联电台 (XHHV) 就波长 K.C.780 问题发生纠纷的来信。

由警司洛根撰写，由 C. Crawford 转呈。

关于随附的日期为1938年12月10日、由浅野少校致工部局警务处的信件，涉及美国人 P.H. Vanmeter 先生所有的美国商业广播电台 (XMHE) 与友联广播电台 (XHHV) 之间因采用相同载波频率波长（即 K.C. 780）而产生的纠纷，有关该纠纷产生方式的详细情况已记录在案，见随附的特科报告中分别列于这两家电台标题下的内容。

简而言之，情况如下：-
Vanmeter 先生于1938年11月11日致信特科，宣布他在迈尔西爱路36号97弄建立了一个广播电台 (XMHE)，频率为 K.C. 780。经查询，Vanmeter 先生对该电台的所有权已在美国总领事馆正式注册。在 Vanmeter 先生的电台建立时，无论是广播监理处还是友联电台 (XHHV) 均未收到其开始广播的通知。然而，需要提及的是，友联电台曾于1938年4月暂停广播，并于1938年10月3日申请重新开放电台。根据警方与日方达成的协议，友联电台管理层被告知，在申请获批之前，必须获得日方的许可，但友联电台拒绝与日方接触，此事遂被搁置。

Japanese were using him as an instrument to embarass the
Sun Sun Station, Mr. Vanmeter refused to change his wave-
length and inserted a notice in the Sin Wan Pao announcing
his intention to broadcast over K.C. 780.

In the light of the foregoing it would appear that
priority of right to use K.C. 780 rests with Mr. Vanmeter.

与此同时，Vanmeter 先生与日本当局进行了一些讨论，结果前者应后者要求，同意在将其电台迁至湖北路131号远东饭店266室的新址后，将波长从 K.C. 780 改为 K.C. 800。然而，在变更实施之前，Vanmeter 先生得知 K.C. 800 是申声电台的波长，而该机构一直未在日方注册。意识到日方正利用他作为使申声电台陷入困境的工具后，Vanmeter 先生拒绝更改波长，并在《新闻报》上刊登公告，宣布他打算通过 K.C. 780 进行广播。

鉴于上述情况，使用 K.C. 780 的优先权似乎属于 Vanmeter 先生。

Re Chung Mei Radio Station(中美電台)
Application was received from the Chung Mei Radio
Station from the licensee P.T. Vanmeter, an American
subject, in the form of a letter dated November 11, 1938
giving the following particulars.
Name .................... Chung Mei Radio Station
Call signal ............. X. M. H. E.
Carrier frequency ....... 780 K.C.
Power ................... 100 W.
Upon receipt of the above application, Vanmeter was
sent for and it was explained to him that the carrier
frequency of 780 K.C. has already been granted to the Yuh
Lien Radio Station which is scheduled to commence operations
soon and on these ground he was advised to make another
application this time for the registration of carrier
frequency of 800 K.C. This was complied with and the
permit was granted by us on November 30, 1938. In spite
of the foregoing, an advertisement was inserted in the
Sin Wan Pao, dated December 8, 1938, announcing that a
trial broadcast will be made by this station as from
December 10, with the carrier frequency of 780 K.C. and
200 W. No reference, whatever has been made to us about
these changes announced in the paper. This station was
called up on the phone and warned to suspend operations,
but our warning was ignored. Consequently, a letter of
warning was addressed to this station advising it to abide
by the permit granted by us and carry on business with
carrier frequency of 800 K.C. and power of 100 W under pain
of rescinding of permit and suspension of business. Apart
from this another letter was sent to the Consul-General for
the United States requesting him to use his influence to
counsel Vanmeter to revert to the original stipulations
and yet another communication was addressed to the Consul-
pages.zh:
(2)
关于中美電台（Chung Mei Radio Station）
中美電台持照人、美国公民 P.T. Vanmeter 提交了一封日期为1938年11月11日的信函提出申请，其中列明以下详情：
名称 .................... 中美電台
呼号 ............. X. M. H. E.
载波频率 ....... 780 K.C.
功率 ................... 100 W.
收到上述申请后，传讯了 Vanmeter 并向他解释，780 K.C. 的载波频率已授予即将开始运营的友聯電台，基于此理由，建议他另行申请注册 800 K.C. 的载波频率。他遵从了这一建议，我局遂于1938年11月30日颁发了许可证。尽管有前述情况，该台却在1938年12月8日的《新闻报》（Sin Wan Pao）上刊登广告，宣布该台将于12月10日起使用 780 K.C. 的载波频率和 200 W 的功率进行试播。对于报纸上宣布的这些变更，该台未向我局作任何说明。我局通过电话传唤该台并警告其停止运营，但我们的警告被无视。因此，我局致函该台发出警告，要求其遵守我局颁发的许可证，在 800 K.C. 载波频率和 100 W 功率下开展业务，否则将面临吊销许可证及停业的风险。此外，另致函美国总领事，请求其施加影响，劝告 Vanmeter 回归原有规定；还有一封信函致日本总领事——

pages.en:
(3)

General for Japan with the request that an official
letter be addressed to the Consul-General for the United
States on the same subject.

In spite of these circumstances, a letter was re-
ceived to-day by the Yan Lien Radio Station from the
Chung Mei Radio Station threatening to institute legal
proceedings against any encroachment on the right
exercised by the latter station registered with the
local American Consulate-General under carrier frequency
of 750 K.C. The communication concluded by saying that
this station would not recognise any authorities with
the exception of the American Government and the Kuomintang
Government of China.

In view of the ridiculous argument advanced by this
licensee coupled with the threats implied in the letter,
we have come to the conclusion that this man is out to
defy the authority of this administration and acting on
the necessity of exercising control over wave-length,
we have been compelled to install a machine in the
broadcasting room of the Yan Lien Station for the purpose
of castigating the Chung Mei Station by means of broad-
casting a special wave.

We remain,

Dear Sirs,

Yours faithfully,

Superintendent.

总领事，请求其就同一事项向美国总领事发出正式信函。

尽管有上述情况，友聯電台今日收到中美電台来信，威胁要对任何侵犯后者权利的行为提起法律诉讼，声称后者已在当地美国总领事馆注册，使用 750 K.C. 的载波频率。该信函结尾称，该台不承认除美国政府和中国国民党政府以外的任何当局。

鉴于该持照人提出的荒谬论点以及信函中隐含的威胁，我们得出结论，此人意在挑战本局的权威；出于行使波长控制权的必要，我们被迫在友聯電台的广播室安装了一台机器，旨在通过发射特殊波段来惩罚中美電台。

此致，

敬启者，

谨上，

总监。

Radio Broadcast Control Administration.
November 30, 1938.

Police Department,
S. M. C.

Dear Sirs,

Re Disposal of Unregistered Radio Stations

Ever since the establishment of this administration
in March this year, five radio stations, namely, Hua Tung
(華東), Dah Loh(大陸), Tung Pong(東方), Poh Ing
(佛音), and Sun Sun (新新), operating in the Inter-
national Settlement, have been warned time and again to
effect registration with this office.

In spite of these warnings, however, the stations
in question continue to broadcast. Such an action on
the part of these stations are not only detrimental to
the prestige of this administration, but also tends to
disrupt the system of control over the wave length and
in view of these circumstances, final letters of warning
were addressed to the stations concerned on November 5 this
year in an attempt to bring about reflection on their
mistaken attitude, but without avail.

As no sign of repentance has been forthcoming, we
have now struck off their names from the list acting on
the assumption that these stations have automatically
forfeited the right of broadcasting enjoyed under legally
established control by their refusal to acknowledge this
system.

The carrier frequencies formerly assumed by these
delinquent stations have already been granted by us to
certain Japanese and foreign radio stations duly registered
with this administration and we take this opportunity to
advise you of these changes for your information.

Yours faithfully,
(Sgd:) Kazuo Asano,
Superintendent.

Certified true copy
H. C. Cordley
TY/.
pages.zh:
无线电广播管制局。
1938年11月30日。

致：
上海公共租界工部局警务处。

敬启者：

关于处置未注册电台事宜

自今年三月本局成立以来，在华界国际租界内运营的五家电台，即華東（Hua Tung）、大陸（Dah Loh）、東方（Tung Pong）、佛音（Poh Ing）和新新（Sun Sun），已被多次警告须向本局办理注册。

然而，尽管有这些警告，有关电台仍继续广播。这些电台的行为不仅损害了本局的威信，而且倾向于破坏波长控制系统；鉴于这种情况，今年11月5日向有关电台发出了最后警告信，试图促使其反思其错误态度，但未获成效。

由于未见悔意，我们现在假定这些电台因拒绝承认这一制度而自动丧失了依法建立的管制下享有的广播权，从而将其名称从名单中除名。

这些违规电台原先占用的载波频率已由我局授予某些已向本局正式注册的日本及外国电台，借此机会告知贵处这些变更，以供查考。

谨上，
（签署：）浅野一雄（Kazuo Asano），
总监。

核证无误副本
H. C. Cordley
TY/.

Reference the attached letter, dated 30-11-38,
addressed by Major Asano, Japanese Broadcasting

the five stations referred to are as follows:-
(1) Hwa Tung (華東)
(2) Dah Loh (大陸)
(3) Tung Fong (東方)
(4) Foh Ying (佛音)
(5) Sun Sun (新新)

These stations were operating locally, prior to
the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities in August,
1937, on permits issued by the National Government of
China. After the fall of Shanghai to the Japanese Forces,
these stations together with several other stations
voluntarily closed down as a temporary measure. Shortly
afterwards, many of the Stations, including the five
mentioned above, resumed broadcasting, several of them
having in the meantime registered with the Japanese
Broadcasting Superintendence Office, Hardoon Building,
Nanking Road, which was established by the Japanese
Military with a view to controlling broadcasting in
Shanghai. At the time in question, besides the five
Stations mentioned above, two other Stations, namely,
Lee Lee (利利) and Tung Loh (東陸) abstained from
registering with the Japanese, while several other Stations,
rather than register with the Japanese or continue to

关于“处置未注册电台”主题的浅野少校1938年11月30日来信
------------------------------------------------------------

参照附件中日期为1938年11月30日、由日本广播监理办公室浅野少校致上海公共租界工部局警务处的关于“处置未注册电台”主题的信件，所涉五家电台如下：
(1) 華東 (Hwa Tung)
(2) 大陸 (Dah Loh)
(3) 東方 (Tung Fong)
(4) 佛音 (Foh Ying)
(5) 新新 (Sun Sun)

这些电台在1937年8月中日敌对行动爆发前，凭中国政府颁发的许可证在当地运营。在上海沦陷于日军之后，这些电台与其他几家电台一起作为临时措施自愿关闭。不久之后，包括上述五台在内的许多电台恢复了广播，其中几家在此期间已向位于南京路哈同大楼的日本广播监理办公室注册，该办公室由日本军方设立，旨在控制上海的广播。当时，除了上述五家电台外，另有两家电台，即利利（Lee Lee）和東陸（Tung Loh），拒绝向日方注册，而其他几家电台则宁愿关闭也不愿向日方注册或在当前局势下继续——

With a view to compelling the seven Stations in
question to register with the Superintendence Office, the
Japanese published notices in the vernacular press and
sent copies of the notices to the Stations through the
post, on at least two occasions, intimating that failure
to register would involve the forfeiture of the right to
broadcast. The S.M.P. also were requested by the Japanese
Authorities to take measures (1) to persuade the
recalcitrant stations to register or (2) to order them
to suspend broadcasting, in letters dated 20-6-38 and
29-6-38. (flagged) The matter was referred to the
Commissioner of Police whose views on the subject are
stated in memos dated 31-5-38 and 16-6-38 respectively,
addressed to the D.C. (Japanese) both of which are quoted
hereunder:-

Memo dated 31-5-38

D.C. (Japanese),

I have already ordered

be permitted. If however, they do operate
and have a permit from the Japanese
authorities we will obtain a guarantee
from them. "A" is covered by the above.
As to "B", I have no power
to go outside the Council's policy but
Special Branch will listen to these Stations

为了迫使这七家有关电台向监理办公室注册，日本人至少在两次在中文报刊上刊登公告，并通过邮政将公告副本发送给各电台，暗示如果不注册将导致丧失广播权。日本当局还在1938年6月20日和1938年6月29日的信函中要求上海公共租界工部局警务处采取措施 (1) 劝说顽固电台注册，或 (2) 命令其停止广播。（标记）此事已转呈警务总监，其对此事的观点分别陈述在1938年5月31日和1938年6月16日致副总监（日方事务）的备忘录中，两者均引述如下：

1938年5月31日备忘录

致副总监（日方事务），

我已下令
(1) 明确规定不允许新电台成立。但是，如果它们确实运营并持有日本当局的许可证，我们将获得它们的保证。“A”类涵盖在上述规定之内。
至于“B”类，我无权超越工部局的政策，但特别处将经常监听这些电台，一旦发现任何反日活动，将根据提交并存案于特别处的保证书立即予以关闭。这是我所能做的最好安排。

quite clear and without Council's instructions
I cannot go further. I think by listening

of the unregistered.

On June 29, 1938, Mr. Hidaka, Japanese Consul-
General called upon the Chairman of the S.M.C. and handed
the latter a memorandum, dated Japanese Consulate-General,
June 29th, 1938, on the subject of Broadcasting Control in
the Shanghai area, with particular reference to Stations
not registered with the Japanese. An excerpt from page
three (flagged) is quoted hereunder:-

"The intention of the Office is anything but to
disregard the licensed rights of the existing
Stations, as may be clear from the following
explanation of its aim and policy.
(1) The aim of the Broadcast Superintendence
Office is to prevent the confusion of
broadcast/electric waves in and around
Shanghai, as well as to restrict the
broadcast items that may disturb peace
and order or hamper the military operation
of the Japanese forces. The Office has no
intention of disregarding arbitrarily the
rights already acquired by the existing
Stations."

One of the seven Stations which failed to register
with the Japanese when the latter assumed control of
broadcasting locally, namely, the Lee Lee Station, registered
with the Japanese Office on November 14, 1938. Another of
the seven Stations, namely, the Tung Loh (東陸) which
originally refused to register with the Japanese, is not
mentioned along with the five referred to in Major Asano's
letter, dated November 30, 1938. It is not known whether
this Station has effected registration with the Japanese
but its omission from the letter mentioned would suggest
that it has arrived at some arrangement with the Japanese.

1938年6月16日备忘录
副总监（日本事务）。

我认为我5月31日的便函已十分清楚，若无工部局指示，我无法采取进一步行动。我认为通过监听，特务处或许能取缔部分未注册的电台。

1938年6月29日，日本总领事日高先生拜访了上海公共租界工部局总董，并向其递交了一份日期为1938年6月29日、由日本总领事馆发出的关于上海地区广播管制的备忘录，特别提及未向日本方面注册的电台。现摘录其中第三页（已做标记）的内容如下：

“本局之意绝非无视现有电台的许可权利，从其目标与政策的以下解释中即可明了。
(1) 广播监理局的目标是防止上海及其周边地区广播电波的混乱，并限制可能扰乱和平秩序或妨碍日军军事行动的广播内容。本局无意任意无视现有电台已取得的权利。”

在日本方面接管当地广播管制时，有七家电台未能向日本方面注册，其中之一即利利（Lee Lee）电台，已于1938年11月14日向日本当局注册。这七家电台中的另一家，即东陆（Tung Loh）电台，起初拒绝向日本方面注册，但在浅野少校1938年11月30日的信函中，并未将其与所提及的五家电台并列。目前尚不知该电台是否已向日本方面完成注册，但既然在上述信函中未予提及，暗示其已与日本方面达成某种安排。

Radio Broadcast Control Administration,
November 30, 1938.

Police Department,
S. M. C.

Dear Sirs,

Re Disposal of Unregistered Radio Stations

Ever since the establishment of this administration
in March this year, five radio stations, namely, Hwa Tung
(華東), Wan Lon(萬隆), Tang Fong(東方), Foh Ing
(佛音), and Sin Sun(新新), operating in the Inter-
national Settlement, have been warned time and again to
effect registration with this office.

In spite of these warnings, however, the stations
in question continue to broadcast. Such an action on
the part of these stations are not only detrimental to
the prestige of this administration, but also tends to
disrupt the system of control over the wave length and
in view of these circumstances, final letters of warning
were addressed to the stations concerned on May 5 this
year in an attempt to bring about reflection on their
mistaken attitude, but without avail.

As no sign of repentance has been forthcoming, we
have now struck off their names from the list acting on
the assumption that these stations have automatically forfeited
forfeited the right of broadcasting enjoyed under legally
established control by their refusal to acknowledge this
system.

The carrier frequencies formerly assumed by these
delinquent stations have already been granted by us to
certain Japanese and foreign radio stations duly registered
with this administration and we take this opportunity to
apprise you of these changes for your information.

Yours faithfully,

Sgd: Kazuo Asano,
Superintendent.

1938年11月30日。

上海公共租界工部局警务处。

敬启者：

关于处置未注册广播电台事宜

自本年三月本局成立以来，位于国际租界内的五家广播电台，即华通（Hwa Tung）、万隆（Wan Lon）、东方（Tang Fong）、佛音（Foh Ing）及新新（Sin Sun），已屡经警告，要求向本局办理注册手续。

尽管有此等警告，上述电台仍继续广播。此类行为不仅有损本局威信，亦扰乱波长管制体系。鉴于此等情况，本局曾于今年5月5日向有关电台发出最后警告信，试图促使其反思其错误态度，但未见成效。

由于未见任何悔过之意，本局现假定这些电台因拒绝承认本管制体系，已自动丧失在合法建立的管制下享有的广播权，故将其名称从名单中除名。

上述违规电台原先占用的载波频率，已由本局授予某些已向本局正式注册的日本及外国广播电台。借此机会，特将此等变更知会贵处，以备查考。

此致

敬礼

签名：浅野一雄（Kazuo Asano），
督察长。

Promulgated on 15.7.33

Regulations Governing Control of Private
Radio Transmission Stations

Art. 1.- Those engaged in broadcasting dialogue and music
by means of radio transmission instrument shall be known,
in general, as radio transmission station (hereafter
abbreviated as broadcasting station) and the installation
and operation of such stations are be subject to the
control of these regulations.

Art. 2.- Any person who is desirous of establishing a
broadcasting station shall first submit an application
to the Radio Transmission Control Station Office (here-
after to be referred to as Control Office).

Art. 3.- The licensee of the broadcasting station shall
furnish the following particulars in the application:
(1) Name of the society or organization, nature of the
organization, address and the name of the licensee.
(2) The object of the establishment of a broadcasting
station.
(3) Name of the broadcasting station, its organization
general
and its/budgetary statement.
(4) Detailed statement regarding the mechanical con-
struction and installation of the broadcasting machine
to be accompanied by illustrations.
(5) Location of the broadcasting station and the studio.

Art. 4.- In the event of the application being approved,
the Control Office shall issue a permit for the installation
work to be commenced. No installation work shall be
undertaken by the broadcasting station until the receipt
of the permit.

Art. 5.- The permit for installation work shall be
valid for 3 months from the date of issue, however, should
the applicant wish to apply for an extension due to some
special circumstances, an additional one month's extension
shall be granted provided that such application is submitted

私人无线电发射台管制条例

第一条.- 凡利用无线电发射仪器广播对话及音乐者，统称为无线电发射台（以下简称广播电台），此类电台的安装及运营须受本条例管制。

第二条.- 凡欲设立广播电台者，须首先向无线电发射管制站办公室（以下简称管制办公室）提出申请。

第三条.- 广播电台执照申请人须在申请书中提供下列详情：
(1) 社团或组织名称、组织性质、地址及执照持有人姓名。
(2) 设立广播电台之目的。
(3) 广播电台名称、其一般组织架构及预算说明书。
(4) 关于广播机器机械构造及安装的详细说明，并附插图。
(5) 广播电台及演播室所在地。

第四条.- 如申请获准，管制办公室将颁发许可证，方可开始安装工作。广播电台在未收到许可证之前，不得进行任何安装工作。

第五条.- 安装工作许可证自签发之日起有效期为三个月，然而，若申请人因特殊情况希望申请延期，只要在该申请不迟于第一份许可证到期前两周提交，则可准予额外延长一个月。

art. 18.- Functions of a broadcasting stations shall be
limited to the following items. The programme, however,
shall be subject to modification or restriction at the
discretion of the Control Office.
(1) Lectures and other addresses beneficial to the
general public.
(2) News item.
(3) Music, play, entertainment, etc.
(4) Commercial advertisement.
Art. 19.- The Control Office shall have access, at all
time, to all the books kept by the broadcasting stations
and shall also inspect the installation when necessary.
Any report or documents called for by the Control Office
shall be forwarded by the management.
Art. 20.- The broadcasting station shall abide by the
following stipulations set forth by the Control Office:
(1) That no station shall resort to such act calculated
to disturb the business of other stations.
(2) That no station shall broadcast or disseminate
news or reports lacking confirmation.
(3) That no station shall exceed the limit of advertise-
ment requirements and unnecessarily engage in dispatching
message or signal to ■ specified listeners.
(4) That no station shall broadcast speech, report,
play or news that are likely to disturb peace and order
and traditional good customs.

any of the articles provided in the foregoing regulations

第十六条.- 所有广播电台应每隔约10分钟播报/其呼号及载波频率。

第十七条.- 所有无线电评论员和技术人员应具备监理处规定的资格。

第十八条.- 广播电台的功能应限于以下项目。然而，节目内容须服从监理处的酌情修改或限制。
(1) 有益于公众的讲座和其他演讲。
(2) 新闻事项。
(3) 音乐、戏剧、娱乐等。
(4) 商业广告。

第十九条.- 监理处应有权随时查阅广播电台保存的所有账簿，并在必要时检查设备。管理处应转发监理处要求的任何报告或文件。

第二十条.- 广播电台应遵守监理处制定的下列规定：
(1) 任何电台不得采取旨在干扰其他电台业务的行为。
(2) 任何电台不得广播或传播未经证实的新闻或报道。
(3) 任何电台不得超过广告要求的限度，并无必要地向■特定听众发送信息或信号。
(4) 任何电台不得广播可能扰乱治安和传统良俗的演讲、报道、戏剧或新闻。

第二十一条.- 任何广播电台如发现违反上述规章中的任何条款，将根据指控的严重程度受到处罚。

JAPANESE CONSULATE-GENERAL,
Shanghai.
June 29, 1938.

1. On March 30, 1938, it was announced in the name of
the Japanese Military authorities that, by reason of the
military necessity for the Japanese forces operating in
Central China, the Broadcast Superintendence Office was
established to take over the superintendence on radio
broadcast formerly exercised by the National Government,
and that the said Office would control broadcast items
and electric waves for the purpose of preventing the
confusion of electric waves in and around Shanghai, as
well as restricting broadcast items that may disturb
peace and order or may hamper the operations of the
Japanese forces.

2. With the above end in view, the Office issued a
notification on March 30, 1938, by which all existing
radio broadcasting stations in Shanghai were informed
to have the necessary particulars registered with the
Office by April 15. Many of the stations, however,
refused the registration and assumed an attitude of non-
cooperation with the Office, except the following nine
stations.

1. Hua-hsing (華興 )
2. Kuo-hua (國華 )
3. Hang-yeh (航業 )
4. Chung-hsi (中西 )
5. Ming-yuan (明遠)

was obtained, although negotiations were conducted repeated-

registration expired on April 27, all the non-registered

- 3 -

3. As above-stated, there have come into existence
two opposing groups of radio stations, registered and
non-registered, and it is feared that the situation may
take a serious turn if left unremedied. The Office
earnestly desires the cooperation of all the parties
concerned, including the Municipal Council, so that a
solution agreeable to all may be attained. The intention
of the Office is anything but to disregard the licensed
rights of the existing stations, as may be clear from the
following explanation of its aim and policy.
(1) The aim of the Broadcast Superintendence Office is to
prevent the confusion of broadcast electric waves in
and around Shanghai, as well as to restrict the broad-
cast items that may disturb peace and order or hamper
the military operation of the Japanese forces. The
Office has no intention of disregarding arbitrarily
the rights already acquired by the existing stations.
It is only for the above-mentioned purposes that the
Office has demanded the registration of the existing
stations therewith.
(2) Neither registration fee nor guarantee money will be
required in any case.
(3) The Office will control the allotment of wave-length,
but will respect the wave-length attributed actually
to the existing stations.
(4) The establishment of a new station requires as a
matter of principle firstly a permission of the Office,
and a permission of the Municipal Council or other
administrative authorities may also be required to
start the broadcast. But the Office will not, in
principle, permit in future the establishment of a
new station, in order to protect the electric waves,
which are already confused, from further confusion.
4. Such being the case, the Municipal Council is
pages.zh:
- 3 -

3. 如上所述，出现了注册和非注册两组对立的广播电台，如果听任这种状况发展而不加补救，恐怕局势会变得严重。该处恳切希望包括工部局在内的所有有关方面予以合作，以便达成各方都能接受的解决方案。从其目标和政策的以下解释中可以清楚地看出，该处绝非意图无视现有电台的执照权利。
(1) 广播监理处的目标是防止上海及其周边地区广播电波的混乱，并限制可能扰乱治安或妨碍日军军事行动的广播内容。该处无意任意无视现有电台已经获得的权利。该处要求现有电台向其登记，仅是出于上述目的。
(2) 在任何情况下均不收取登记费或保证金。
(3) 该处将控制波长的分配，但会尊重现有电台实际使用的波长。
(4) 原则上，设立新电台首先需获得该处的许可，开始广播可能还需要工部局或其他行政当局的许可。但是，为了保护已经混乱的电波不再进一步混乱，该处原则上将来不会允许设立新电台。
4. 鉴于此，工部局

Radio Broadcasting Control Station
June 25, 1938.

Police Department,
S. M. C.

Re: Granting of Permit to Dah Ya Radio
Station to Reopen

Sirs,

It will be recalled that some time ago this
office requested you to seal up the Dah Ya Radio Station
(大亞電台), 945 Sikiang Road, for failing to effect
registration in accordance with the order issued by this
office and also refusing to discontinue to operate in
spite of our order to do so which had been obeyed by
other stations. Meanwhile, however, this policy was
strongly condemned at the meeting of shareholders held
recently and they also unanimously decided to dismiss the
former manager named Kuo Sun Hsiang (郭順香) and
substitute him with a Chinese lawyer named Soong Ts Haiang
(宋士驤) who has been appointed manager to succeed
Kuo.

It is now evident that the management sincerely
regret the past error and the new manager Mr. Soong has
called at this office several times tendering apologies
for disobedience of order in the past.

In view of these circumstances, we write this letter
to request you to grant permission to this radio station
to reopen when the management approach you with the
permit already issued by us.

Yours faithfully,

Sgd: Kazuwo Agano.

May 20, 1938.

Mr. Uyehara,
Deputy Commissioner,
Shanghai Municipal Police.

Dear Sir,

I beg to express my sincere thanks for
proper measures adopted by the Shanghai Municipal
Council in connection with the suspension of
business of the Dah Ya (大亞) and the Dah Kwong Ming
(大光明) Broadcasting Stations as requested to the
Commissioner of Police through you.

I response to your queries of the 20th
instant on the subject of the operation of new
broadcasting stations, I beg to inform you as follows:-

Having been informed of your decision to
reject the applications forwarded to you by the Dah
Lai (大來) and the Wing Sung (永生) Broadcasting
Stations, I have pleasure in taking note of the outcome.

The aforementioned two stations as well
as the Chin Ying (金鷹) Broadcasting Stations registered
with this office prior to the expiration of the date of
registration. Applications for construction had already
been received from them and permits were given accordingly.
The Dah Lai and the Chin Ying Stations reported sometime
ago that they had completed the work. Upon making
technical examination some defects were found in the
work and they were told to undergo re-examination.
If the work is found satisfactory after re-examination
it is the policy of this office to give them permission
to operate.

May 30, 1938.

Commissioner of Police.

With reference to the attached official
letter from Major Asano, Officer in charge of the
Broadcasting Control Office, I have to inform you
that after a series of conversations with him who
officially represents the Japanese interested parties
concerning the broadcasting in Shanghai as well as
the occupied areas, I am given to understand that
the Japanese authorities have a strong view in
connection with the complete control of the broad-
casting in the air above Shanghai and necessary
steps should therefore be taken in regard to com-
pulsory registration of all Chinese Stations.

Although further negotiations have not
yet officially been opened for reconsideration on
this subject, I strongly suggest that due consideration
be entertained to meet the Japanese requests within
the jurisdiction of the S.M.P. with a spirit of
co-operation and mutual understanding which are greatly
needed under the existing circumstances.

In view of the above, I request that the
following steps be carried out pending negotiations.

(1) No new applications should be accepted,
unless a permit obtained from the Broad-
casting Control Office be shown together
with application.

1938年5月30日。

警务总监。

兹提及附上的由广播管制办公室主任浅野少校发出的公函，我必须通知您，在与他进行了一系列会谈后——他官方代表日本有关方面，涉及上海及占领区的广播事宜——我了解到，日本当局对于完全控制上海上空广播持有强烈观点，因此应采取必要步骤，强制所有中国广播电台进行注册。

尽管尚未就此议题的重新考虑正式开启进一步谈判，但我强烈建议，在当前局势下亟需合作与相互理解的精神下，应在上海公共租界工部局警务处的管辖范围内，充分考虑以满足日方的要求。

鉴于上述情况，我要求在谈判期间执行以下步骤。

(1) 除非在申请时出示从广播管制办公室获得的许可证，否则不应接受任何新申请。

to operate.

除上述三家电台外，另有三家电台，即“上海”（Shanghai）、“精美”（Chin Mei）和“杨氏”（Yang Sz），已向本办公室注册并正在建设中。若它们通过必要的检查，我方政策也是予以许可。目前仅向上述六家电台颁发许可证，不再颁发其他许可证。若上述六家电台在获得本办公室的正式许可证后提交申请，希望贵方在进行必要的警务调查（暂不进行技术检查）并与我方保持联系后，决定是否颁发许可证。
从控制电波的角度来看，令人遗憾的是，下列六家广播电台，即新新（The Sun Sun）、利利（Lee Lee）、通洛（Tong Lo）、大洛（Dah Lo）、富音（Voo Yin）和华通（Hwa Tong），拒绝向本办公室注册，却仅凭贵方的许可继续运营。
据确认，这些电台具有反日倾向，请贵方以适当的理由采取措施暂停这些电台的广播，以防止未来发生麻烦。

盖章：浅野，广播管制办公室主任。

pages.en:
Copy.
May 20, 1938.

Mr. Uyehara,
Deputy Commissioner,
Shanghai Municipal Police.

Dear Sir,

I beg to express my sincere thanks for
proper measures adopted by the Shanghai Municipal
Council in connection with the suspension of
business of the Dah Ya (大亚) and the Dah Kwong Ming
(大光明) Broadcasting Stations as requested to the
Commissioner of Police through you.

I response to your queries of the 20th
instant on the subject of the operation of new
broadcasting stations, I beg to inform you as follows:-

Having been informed of your decision to
reject the applications forwarded to you by the Dah
Lai (大来) and the Wing Sung (永生) Broadcasting
Stations, I have pleasure in taking note of the outcome.

The aforementioned two stations as well
as the Chin Ying (金鹰) Broadcasting Stations registered
with this office prior to the expiration of the date of
registration. Applications for construction had already
been received from them and permits were given accordingly.
The Dah Lai and the Chin Ying Stations reported sometime
ago that they had completed the work. Upon making
technical examination, some defects were found in the
work and they were told to undergo re-examination.
If the work is found satisfactory after re-examination
it is the policy of this office to give them permission
to operate.
pages.zh:
副本。
1938年5月20日。

上原先生，
副总监，
上海公共租界工部局警务处。

尊敬的先生：

谨就通过您向警务总监提出的关于暂停大亚（Dah Ya）和大光明（Dah Kwong Ming）广播电台业务之请求，对上海公共租界工部局所采取的适当措施，表示诚挚的谢意。

针对贵方本月20日就新广播电台运营事宜提出的查询，谨答复如下：-

获悉贵方决定驳回转呈给您的大来（Dah Lai）和永生（Wing Sung）广播电台的申请，我方乐见这一结果。

上述两家电台以及金鹰（Chin Ying）广播电台均在注册截止日期前向本办公室办理了注册。此前已收到它们的建设申请，并据此颁发了许可证。大来电台和金鹰电台于前段时间报告称工程已完工。经技术检查，发现工程存在一些缺陷，已告知其接受复查。若复查后工程令人满意，本办公室的政策是准许其运营。

pages.en:
- 2 -

Apart from the above three stations there are
three more stations, i.e. the "Shanghai" (之江),
the "Chin Mei" (精美) and the "Yang Su" (样苏),
which have already registered with this office and are
under construction. It is also our policy to give them
permission should they pass the necessary examination.
For the present permits will be issued only to the
above six stations and no further permits will be issued.
If applications be forwarded by the afore-mentioned
six stations, after having received formal permit from
this office, it is to be hoped that you will make
necessary police inquiries, setting aside technical
examination, and after keeping in touch with me, decide
whether or not to issue permit.
It is matter for regret from the point of view of
controlling the electric wave that the following six
broadcasting stations, i.e. The Sun Sun (新新), the
Lee Lee (利利), the Tong Lo (东隆), the Dah Lo (大隆),
the Voo Yin (佛音) and the Hwa Tong (华东), which
have refused to register with this office, still continue
to operate with your permission only.
It is affirmed that these stations have anti-Japanese
leaning and you are requested to take measures to suspend
broadcasting by these stations on some suitable ground
so as to prevent trouble arising in the future.

Sealed: Asano, Chief of the
Broadcasting Control Office.

Certified true copy.

May 30, 1938.

Commissioner of Police.

With reference to the attached official
letter from Major Asano, Officer in charge of the
Broadcasting Control Office, I have to inform you
that after a series of conversations with him who
officially represents the Japanese interested parties
concerning the broadcasting in Shanghai as well as
the occupied areas, I am given to understand that
the Japanese authorities have a strong view in
connection with the complete control of the broad-
casting in the air above Shanghai and necessary
steps should therefore be taken in regard to com-
pulsory registration of all Chinese Stations.

Although further negotiations have not
yet officially been opened for reconsideration on
this subject, I strongly suggest that due consideration
be entertained to meet the Japanese requests within
the jurisdiction of the S.M.P. with a spirit of
co-operation and mutual understanding which are greatly
needed under the existing circumstances.

In view of the above, I request that the
following steps be carried out pending negotiations.

(1) No new applications should be accepted,
unless a permit obtained from the Broad-
casting Control Office be shown together
with application.
pages.zh:
1938年5月30日。

致警务总监。

关于附上的由负责广播管制办公室的浅野少校发出的公函，我必须通知您，在与他就上海及占领区广播问题代表日本相关利益方进行一系列会谈后，我了解到日本当局对于完全控制上海上空广播持有强烈观点，因此应采取必要步骤，对所有中国电台实行强制注册。

虽然尚未就此主题的重新考量正式开启进一步谈判，但我强烈建议，在目前急需合作与相互理解的情况下，应在上海公共租界工部局警务处的管辖范围内，充分考虑以满足日方要求。

鉴于上述情况，我要求在谈判期间执行以下步骤。

(1) 除非在申请时出示从广播管制办公室获得的许可证，否则不得接受任何新申请。

pages.en:
- 2 -

(2) "A" should be accepted and a closer
co-operation be fostered.
(3) "B" should be considered and necessary
measures be taken, otherwise smooth
relationship between us will not be
obtained.

(Sd.) S. Uyehara.

Deputy Commissioner (Japanese)

Certified true copy.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

(2) 应接受“A”，并加强更紧密的合作。
(3) 应考虑“B”并采取必要措施，否则我们将无法维持顺畅的关系。

（签名）S. Uyehara。

副总监（日籍）

核证无误副本。

（总部）办公笔记
日期 1938年5月13日

P. A.
S I

新广播电台

(a) 在功率尺寸问题解决之前，无需建立或允许任何新电台运营

(b) 达成协议后，在以下情况满足之前，不得允许电台开播：
(1) 它们有财务保证，以确保其地位如目前所示？
(2) 它们就最低覆盖范围的一点达成一致：-
(A.) 我们是否获得一份附属的书面信函
(B) 遵守关于解决由此产生的纠纷的北平指示。

另外两点包含在“中国政府当局 - 原则上”
“若同意某电台，则地方当局”
予以省略。在此类情况下，我们现有的条款需要更改为/或与 (2) 达成协议，除非电台已被关闭。

D C (J)
秘书

pages.en:
CONFIDENTIAL

May 13, 1938.

D. C. (Special Branch).

Referring to our conversation this
morning, I informed the Japanese authorities
that the two broadcasting stations were suspended
by you indefinitely, on what grounds I did not
disclose. They accepted the information with
pleasure. I also suggested them that a fresh
talk in connection with the broadcasting be
started without delay.

I strongly request that the two
stations and any new ones be not permitted to
function pending further negotiations between
the two parties.

D. C. (Japanese)
pages.zh:
机密

1938年5月13日。

致 D. C. （特务科）。

参照我们今天早晨的谈话，我已通知日本当局，这两家广播电台已被贵方无限期暂停，但我未透露具体理由。他们愉快地接受了这一信息。我还向他们建议，应立即开始就广播问题进行新的会谈。

我强烈要求，在两方进一步谈判期间，不得允许这两家电台及任何新电台运作。

D. C. （日籍）

REPORT
Date May 10, 1938.
Subject Control of Chinese Radio Broadcasting Stations.
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by [手写签名]

Reference the instructions of the Commissioner
of Police on Memo. dated May 6, 1938, addressed by the
Acting Secretary, S.M.C. to the Commissioner of Police,
on the above subject, the responsible persons of all the
Chinese Radio Broadcasting Stations located within the
Settlement were interviewed at Special Branch Headquarters
on May 8, 1938, and again warned against broadcasting
anti-Japanese or other political propaganda upon penalty
of closure of their stations in the event of disobedience
of Police orders. The person responsible for each
respective station undertook to comply with the warning
issued by the Police and in pledge of their good faith
re-chopped the original guarantee supplied to the Police.
A list of the stations warned with details of registration
applications, guarantees, etc. is attached hereto.

Shanghai. May 6, 19 38.

The Commissioner of Police.

Control of Chinese Radio Broadcasting Stations.

I have to inform you that the Council reached the
decision in meeting last night that the Police Department be

radio broadcasting stations in the above sense, upon penalty
of closure of their stations in the event of disobedience of
Police orders.

Acting Secretary.

REPORT

Subject Translation of extract from Ta Lei Pao, dated 6/5/38, entitled
"Broadcasting May Be Resumed May 10."

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by

Reference the attached translation of an extract from
the Ta Lei Pao, dated 6/5/38, entitled "Broadcasting May
Be Resumed May 10" it has been learned that between 9.15 p.m.
and 11 p.m. on May 6, 1938, eleven persons claiming to
represent different radio broadcasting stations in Shanghai
held a meeting in the office of the Grand Hotel, 120 Yu Ya
Ching Road. Wong Ding Pah (王定邦), representing the
Foh Ying Radio Station, 128 Museum Road, presided and addressed
the attendance stating that a written reply had been received
from Mr. T.K. Ho, Chinese Deputy Secretary of the S.M.C.,
warning the various radio stations to rigidly suppress anti-
Japanese and political propaganda as well as to cooperate with
the authorities in the maintenance of peace and order in the
Settlement. The reply also pointed out, the chairman of the
meeting continued, that those who failed to comply with the
order of the Council would be compelled to suspend operation.
Discussions subsequently took place and it was decided
that those who recently suspended business as precaution against
possible interference, will resume operation on May 14, 1938.
There are altogether 20 stations (Chinese) situated in
the Settlement and 3 in the French Concession. Nine of the
twenty stations in the Settlement and the three in the French
Concession are not in operation at present. There is no
indication that the stations in the French Concession will
resume operation in the near future.

D.C. (Special Branch)

Ta Mei Fao s-

Broadcasting May Be Resumed May 10

According to information received, the Japanese
have agreed to the principle that Chinese broadcasting
stations need not register with them but should submit to
strict supervision by the S.M.C. and will cease to broadcast
anti-Japanese programmes.
Yesterday the Radio Broadcasting Station Owners'
Association held a meeting at which it was decided that all
stations be immediately restored to the situation existing
prior to April 23. It is probable that all the stations
will be fully restored by May 10.
Those stations which have resumed business have
not registered with the Japanese and have, for business
reasons, continued their service in accordance with the
stipulations laid down by the S.M.C.

广播可能于 5 月 10 日恢复

据收到的消息，日本人已同意以下原则：华资广播电台无需向他们注册，但应接受工部局的严格监管，并将停止广播反日节目。
昨日，广播电台业主协会举行会议，决定所有电台立即恢复到 4 月 23 日之前的状态。所有电台很可能在 5 月 10 日前完全恢复。
那些已恢复营业的电台并未向日本人注册，而是出于商业原因，按照工部局规定的条款继续提供服务。

Hopes that the registration ques-

Council met, and a report read on
this subject, the situation is just

stations registration with Japanese
authorities was first raised.
The Japanese, it is learned, are
showing no inclination to take
forceful measures against stations
which do not comply with the re-
quest for registration, and the
threat of an impending crisis is a
mere rumor. However, the Council is
facing reality, and has requested

through the Shanghai Municipal

Rather than submit to Japanese
control, half of the approximately
20 Chinese radio stations in Shang-

pages.zh:
701

无线电局势
回到原点

关于本地广播电台注册问题将在昨晚的上海工部局董事会上最终解决的希望是毫无根据的。虽然董事会召开了会议，并宣读了有关此问题的报告，但目前的局势与最初提出向日本当局注册电台的问题时并无二致。

据悉，日本人对于未遵从注册要求的电台，并未表现出采取强硬措施的意向，所谓迫在眉睫的危机纯属谣言。然而，董事会正面对现实，并已要求中国“广播电台”通过上海公共租界工部局警务处，避免传播任何可能被贴上反日标签的报道。

与其屈服于日本人的控制，上海约20家中国无线电台中的半数已暂停广播。在其余电台中，一家是中国基督教演播室，将其广播内容限制在宗教题材；另一家则已知持有日本许可证。

另有报道称，由美籍华人在爱文义路（Avenue Road）经营的XMHC电台，于周三收到一份通知，据称该通知严厉要求该电台停止广播，因其无视了要求注册的通知。由于业主为美国公民，XMHC电台已向驻沪美国领事馆注册。据报道，该通知日期为5月3日，由“广播监理处”处长浅野（K. Asano）少佐签署。

April 28, 38.
Chinese Radio Broadcasting Stations : Registration with
Broadcasting Superintendence Office, Room 316, Hardeen
Building, Nanking Road

With reference to Commissioner of Police's memo
dated April 27, 1938 on the subject of a letter addressed
by Mr. K. Asano, Director of Broadcasting Superintendence
Office, Room 316, Hardeen Building, Nanking Road, to the
Secretary-General, S.M.C., in reference to the proposed
registration with the Japanese Controlled Broadcasting
Superintendence Office, of all Chinese Radio Broadcasting
Stations in the Settlement, D.S.I. Logan and D.S. Kumashita,
acting on instructions issued by D.C. (Special Branch),
visited Room 316 aforesaid, at 3 p.m., April 27, 1938, but
were unable to see Mr. Asano, who was stated to be on
business in Hongkew. Mr. Y. Ban (Japanese) who claimed
to be in charge of the Broadcasting Superintendence Office,
directly under Mr. Asano, was informed in terms of the
Commissioner of Police's memo of the extent to which the
S.M.P. is prepared to assist the Broadcasting Superintendence
Office in effecting registration of Chinese Radio Broad-
casting Stations in the Settlement. It was suggested to
Mr. Ban that he should supply forms of application for
registration to the S.M.P. who would undertake to deliver
them to the different Chinese Broadcasting Stations and
after the necessary details had been filled in, collect
and forward them to the Broadcasting Superintendence
Office. The suggestion was at first coldly received
by Mr. Ban who appeared to hold the view that as the
Chinese Stations had ignored all the notifications sent
out by the Japanese on the subject, they had deprived

华资广播电台：在南京路哈丁大楼316室广播监理处注册

鉴于警务处处长1938年4月27日的备忘录，涉及浅野先生（Mr. K. Asano，广播监理处处长，办公地点：南京路哈丁大楼316室）致工部局秘书长的一封信，内容关于租界内所有华资广播电台拟向日方控制的广播监理处注册一事。1938年4月27日下午3时，副督察长洛根和下山副督察根据特别处副处长的指示，访问了上述316室，但未能会见浅野先生，据称其正在虹口处理公务。于是向自称直接受浅野先生领导、负责广播监理处事务的班先生（Mr. Y. Ban，日本人）通报了警务处处长备忘录中关于警务处愿意协助广播监理处办理租界内华资广播电台注册工作的程度。建议班先生向警务处提供注册申请表，警务处将负责将其分发给各华资广播电台，并在填写必要细节后，收集并转交至广播监理处。该建议起初遭到班先生的冷淡对待，他似乎认为，既然华资电台无视日方就此问题发出的所有通知，它们便失去了进一步被考虑的权利，并应受到相应处理。然而，随后他改变了态度，表示对警务处提供协助的形式感到满意，但声称并未准备任何申请表，因此无法向警务处提供。不过，他出示了一份由广播监理处发给所有广播电台的第2号通知副本（无日期，附后），其中列有所需详情的清单，并表示该通知可作为申请表使用，同时交给下山副督察一份上海华资广播电台名单。

April 28, 38.
Chinese Radio Broadcasting Stations : Registration with
Broadcasting Superintendence Office, Room 316, Hardoon
Building, Nanking Road

With reference to Commissioner of Police's memo
dated April 27, 1938 on the subject of a letter addressed
by Mr. K. Asano, Director of Broadcasting Superintendence
Office, Room 316, Hardoon Building, Nanking Road, to the
Secretary-General, S.M.C., in reference to the proposed
registration with the Japanese Controlled Broadcasting
Superintendence Office, of all Chinese Radio Broadcasting
Stations in the Settlement, D.S.I. Logan and D.~. Mimashita,
acting on instructions issued by D.C. (Special Branch),
visited Room 316 aforesaid, at 3 p.m., April 27, 1938, but
were unable to see Mr. Asano, who was stated to be on
business in Hongkew. Mr. Y. Ban (Japanese) who claimed
to be in charge of the Broadcasting Superintendence Office,
directly under Mr. Asano, was informed in terms of the
Commissioner of Police's memo of the extent to which the
S.M.P. is prepared to assist the Broadcasting Superintendence
Office in effecting registration of Chinese Radio Broad-
casting Stations in the Settlement. It was suggested to
Mr. Ban that he should supply forms of application for
registration to the S.M.P. who would undertake to deliver
them to the different Chinese Broadcasting Stations and
after the necessary details had been filled in, collect
and forward them to the Broadcasting Superintendence
Office. The suggestion was at first coldly received
by Mr. Ban who appeared to hold the view that as the
Chinese Stations had ignored all the notifications sent
out by the Japanese on the subject, they had deprived

关于警察总监1938年4月27日就浅野先生（Mr. K. Asano，音译，广播监理处处长，办公地点：南京路哈同大楼316室）致工部局秘书长信函一事发出的备忘录，该信函涉及租界内所有中文广播电台向受日本控制的广播监理处进行拟议注册之事，特别处副总督察洛根（D.S.I. Logan）和**三下**警佐（D.~. Mimashita，原文如此，疑为Kamashita之误，按原文音译为米马希塔或保留原文，此处依指令照实译，但结合上下文应为Kamashita，然原文印作Mimashita或类似乱码，此处暂译为“三下”或保留英文。看后文都是Kamashita。此处原文是 `D.~. Mimashita`，波浪号表示看不清。根据指令4，标原文不清或照实。此处译为“三下（音译，原文不清）”或直接保留。为了流畅，结合后文统一性，极大概率是Kamashita。但指令要求不脑补。我将译为“下田（原文作Mimashita，疑为Kamashita）”或者严格按字面。让我们看p138开头是Kamashita。p137这里是Mimashita。我将译为“下田（原文误作Mimashita）”以符合历史事实同时指出原文问题，或者更稳妥地，译为“三下警佐（D.~. Mimashita，音译）”。不，指令3说能确定的用通行中文。Kamashita是下田。Mimashita不是标准名。我将译为“下田警佐（原文作Mimashita）”。

In connection with Nos. 12 and 13 above, Mr. Ban
of the Broadcasting Superintendence Office, stated that
as these Stations had opened up since April 1, 1938,
without applying for the permission of the Japanese
Authorities, he did not wish to entertain an application
from them for registration and requested the Police to
close them down. He was informed in reply that his
request would be passed to the proper quarter. In this
connection D.S. Kamashita, on the instructions of
D.C. (Special Branch), has been directed to inform
Mr. Ban that he should make any request for assistance
in writing and that both the Stations named are being
treated similarly to the other Stations as they established
their respective concerns with the permission of the S.M.C.
It should be mentioned that the Overseas Broadcasting
Station, Lane 1729, 5 Avenue Road, was included in the
Japanese list of Chinese Broadcasting Stations. This
Station is owned by certain Chinese, one of whom
Mr. Herbert E. Moy, is a U.S.A. naturalized citizen,
and the owner of 60% of the property. Mr. Kahl, of
the local U.S.A. Consulate-General, when interviewed on
April 28, 1938, stated that the Station might be regarded
as being under the protection of the American Authorities
though complete registration has not been effected with
the latter. In this connection D.S. Kamashita was
instructed to inform the Broadcasting Superintendence
Office that the Station is American and not Chinese.

File No. F31/1
POLICE FORCE 27 APR 1938

Translation of letter to Secretary from
Shanghai Association of Privately
Established Radio Broadcasting Stations.
Dated 25th April, 1938.

Broadcasting: Control of

On the 11th instant our members submitted a petition to the
Council enclosing copies of two letters from the so-called
"Radio Broadcasting Supervision Board". Presumably the petition
has received the Council's consideration.

On the 21st instant our members received a further communication
from the Board instructing them to apply for registration not
later than the 27th instant, a copy of these instructions is
enclosed herewith. We hope that in the interest of public peace
and safety, the Council devise measures to deal equitably with
this matter.

(Chopped) Wong Kau-peh,
Chairman of Executive Committee

Translation of enclosure.

Order No.3 issued by the Radio
Broadcasting Supervision Board.

In accordance with our Order No.2 all Broadcasting Stations
must apply for registration before 15th April. This new Order
serves to remind the public that if broadcasting stations fail to
apply for registration before 27th April, they will be considered
as having forfeited all privileges in connection with registration.

(Signed & Chopped) Director

（批：hls 28/4）
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 28 APR. 1938 SPECIAL BRANCH）

档案号 F31/1
警务处 1938年4月27日

上海私立广播电台协会致秘书长的信函译文。
日期：1938年4月25日。

广播：管制事宜

本月11日，本会会员向工部局提交请愿书，并附上所谓“广播监理委员会”两封信件的副本。想必该请愿书已得到工部局的审议。

本月21日，本会会员收到该委员会的进一步函件，指示他们最迟于本月27日申请注册，该指示的副本随函附上。我们希望工部局出于公共和平与安全的利益，制定措施公平处理此事。

Shanghai, 7th April, 1938
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE ... N. F 2900 ...）

Mr. S. Fessenden,
Secretary General,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Shanghai.

Sir,

Re Broadcasting Superintendence in Shanghai.

As perhaps you know this office has taken over the superintendence of broadcasting stations and all the affairs connecting with the control and leadership of broadcasting, which have hitherto been under the supervision of the Communications Bureau of the National Government and Central Executive Committee.

Accordingly we sent Notification No.1 dated 20th ult. to all the broadcasting stations in Shanghai stating the above reasons and consequently despatched Notification No.2 dated 31st. ult. again to make the necessary registration to this office for new permits by the 15th inst., but all of them being failed to make this step, the third has been forwarded effecting to cancel their rights of registration unless they make the above procedure on or before the 27th of this month.

In the above circumstances, we are now compelled to ready to stop the business of those, who break the regulations by a some compulsory means, such as to remove or to break down some important parts of machine.

In such case, we are much obliged if you will kindly co-operate with us sending some policemen to let us to attain our object, or at least not to interfere with our purpose.

Yours faithfully,

K. Asano.
Director of Broadcasting
Superintendence Office.

总秘书，
上海公共租界工部局，
上海。

先生：

关于上海广播监管事宜。

或许您已知悉，本处已接管广播电台的监管工作，以及此前由国民政府交通部及中央执行委员会监督的所有与广播控制和领导相关的事务。

据此，我们于上月20日向上海所有广播电台发出了第1号通知，说明了上述理由；随后又于上月31日再次发出第2号通知，要求各方在本月15日前向本处办理必要的注册手续以换取新许可证。但由于各方均未采取此步骤，现发出第三份通知，规定除非在本月27日或之前完成上述程序，否则将取消其注册权。

鉴于上述情况，我们现在被迫准备采取某些强制手段（如拆除或破坏机器的重要部件）来停止那些违反规定者的业务。

在此情况下，如蒙贵方合作，派遣一些警员协助我们要达成目标，或者至少不干涉我们的行动，我们将不胜感激。

此致，

K. 浅野 (K. Asano)。
广播监管处处长。

these have ascertained the following information.

The above Radio Station commenced to broadcast on
the 1/4/38, from 15 Bubbling Well Road, The New World,
and is owned by the Dah Mei (大美) Radio Supply Company
and the Dah Mei Advertising Agency.

by the S.M.P. but had not been registered with the

made on the 10/4/38.

replied that he had received no instructions for doing
this, neither did he know how to do so, and the unknown

X.M.H.R. 广播电台及注册引发的麻烦。

1938年4月26日下午5时10分，静安寺路15号新世界的大美 (Dah Mei) 广播电台经理梅嶢亭 (May Yeh Ding) 接到一个身份不明的中国人打来的电话，称如果上述广播电台未在1938年4月27日前注册，将会带来麻烦。

上述人员向警方报告，警方随即指示对此案进行调查，并查明了以下信息。

上述广播电台于1938年4月1日开始从静安寺路15号新世界进行广播，归大美 (Dah Mei) 无线电供应公司和大美广告社所有。

经理为梅嶢亭 (May Yeh Ding)，后者称该电台已获上海公共租界警务处 (S.M.P.) 许可运营，但尚未在中国政府注册，尽管已于1938年4月10日提出申请。

在上述时间，那位不知名的打电话者询问了向日本当局注册电台的事宜，经理回答说他没有收到这样做的指示，也不知道该如何做，而那位不知名

Subject XHB. Fuh Ying Radio Broadcasting Station -
cessation of operations.

Made by D.S. Henchman Forwarded by G Crawford I S

On April 15, Station XHB, operated by the Chinese
Buddhist Society, at 418 Hart Road, ceased to function
and rumours were circulated to the effect that the Japanese
Authorities had compelled suspension of operations because
of the refusal of those responsible to register with the
Radio Broadcasting Stations Supervisory Office, Hardoon
Building, Nanking Road.

Enquiries were made at the offices of the station
concerned and it was learnt from Lee Sih-dong, a staff
member, that broadcasts had ceased because the transmitter
was not in working order. Mr. Lee went on to say that
communications had been received from the Radio Broadcasting
Stations Supervisory Office, containing instructions that
the station be registered. These instructions had been
ignored but when the transmitter failed it was decided
that in order to avoid trouble, repairs should not be
effected and the station allowed to remain idle until the
question of registration had been clarified.

SECRETARIAT, B. D. 68/3/6
Date /3 5
April 13, 1938.

To:-
The Secretary-General.
(copies sent to Major Gerrard and Mr.Cobb).

Mr Auge, Acting French Consul-General, telephoned me yesterday
evening just before dinner much concerned at having read in a
"Denoi" report that the Shanghai Municipal Council was allowing
the new Broadcasting supervisory body to function while the
French Concession authorities had refused. I told him that
this was not the position; that the Shanghai Municipal Council
had to-date taken no action--and had neither allowed nor
refused to allow the new organisation to function. We had,
however, requested the Chinese stations to report at once any
interference and we proposed to give police protection. Mr.
Auge seemed re-assured.

I formed the impression that Mr.Auge was anxious about
this subject and hoped that, as far as may be possible, a joint
policy can be pursued.

I pass this message on now in case there are developments
during the holiday.

D.C.B.
This might be placed
on record for
D.S. & Captain
G. Godfrey Phillips
Secretary.

奥热先生（Mr Auge），代理法国总领事，昨晚晚餐前给我打电话，他对在《德诺伊》（"Denoi"，原文不清）报道中读到上海公共租界工部局允许新的广播监管机构运作，而法租界当局却予以拒绝一事，深感关切。我告诉他情况并非如此；上海公共租界工部局迄今未采取任何行动——既未允许也未拒绝允许新组织运作。然而，我们已要求中国电台立即报告任何干扰行为，并打算提供警察保护。奥热先生似乎放心了。

我形成的印象是，奥热先生对此事感到焦虑，并希望尽可能采取联合政策。

我现在转达此信息，以防假期中出现新情况。

F.M.C. Attitude
On Radio Flayed

Refusal Of Japan Plan
To Control Chinese
Stations Hit

Japanese official quarters were
reported yesterday by the Shang-
hai Nippo to be "displeased" by
the adamant refusal of the French
Concession authorities to allow
Japanese control over Chinese
radio broadcasting stations.

The French stand, the daily
declared, was in sharp contrast to
the attitude assumed by the
Shanghai Municipal Council which
informed Chinese stations in the
Settlement that they would be
supervised by any organ that re-
places the local office of the Na-
tionalist Ministry of Communica-
tions.

Operations Control

The Council, however, retained
full control over the actual opera-
tions of these stations, the journal
added.

Chinese broadcasting stations in
the Concession, on the other hand,
were allegedly informed by the
authorities that they need not pay
any attention to the Japanese
notices on the control of broad-
casting.

Moreover, the journal declared
the owners of the Chinese broad-
casting stations were informed by
the Concession authorities that
the latter were opposed to any
contact between these stations and
the Japanese control organ.

To Brighten Broadcast

"It is deeply to be regretted,"
the Nippo said, "that the Conces-
sion authorities have adopted such
an uncompromising attitude, in
the face of the Japanese authori-
ties' desire to brighten up Chinese
broadcasts and to maintain peace
and order in the occupied areas."

Only about 24 stations are in
operation in Shanghai now as
contrasted with about 40 before
the outbreak of the hostilities, the
daily reported.

法租界当局态度
在无线电问题上受到抨击

拒绝日本控制中国
电台的计划受挫

据《上海日报》（Shanghai Nippo）昨日报道，日本官方人士对法租界当局坚决拒绝允许日本控制中国广播电台一事表示“不满”。

该日报宣称，法国的立场与上海公共租界工部局所采取的态度形成鲜明对比，后者通知租界内的中国电台，它们将受任何取代国民政府交通部本地办事处的机构监管。

运营控制

但该报补充说，工部局保留了对这些电台实际运营的完全控制权。

另一方面，据称法租界内的中国广播电台已获当局告知，无需理会日本关于控制广播的通知。

此外，该报宣称，法租界当局已告知中国广播电台业主，法方反对这些电台与日本控制机构有任何接触。

旨在改善广播

《上海日报》称：“令人深感遗憾的是，面对日本当局希望改善中国广播并在占领区维持和平与秩序的愿望，法租界当局采取了如此不妥协的态度。”

该日报报道，目前上海仅有约24家电台在运营，而战事爆发前约有40家。

CHINA DAILY NEWS,
Radio Stations
Requested to
Register

Shanghai Foreign Stations
To Refer Matter to Their
Consulates for Advice.

"We are reporting the matter to our Consulates and will seek their advice before deciding what to do." That was the consensus of answers from some of the foreign radio companies in Shanghai, in reply to questions concerning letters which have been addressed to them by an organization terming itself the "Broadcasting Superintendent's Office." Chinese radio stations have also received this letter, but have not yet come to any decision.

Normally, radio stations in Shanghai are registered with the Ministry of Communications; those in the French Concession are also required to take out a licence issued by the police authorities there. When all Chinese Government offices were closed in Shanghai, as a result of the hostilities, the stations continued to operate, although some of them began to wonder what their position was.

They have now received this letter, which is not signed, but bears a chop of the office in English and Chinese. It is not known whether or not it is a subsidiary organ of the "Ta Tao" City Government, but it gives as its address "Room 316, Hardoon Building." The Japanese censor office is also in the Hardoon Building, on the floor below.

The circular to radio station owners requests them to furnish the usual information required in the past by the Ministry of Communications, such as the name of the owner, power, location and details of the equipment, and the names of the announcers, and in addition requires a copy of the permit issued by the Ministry of Communications and the call-signal issued by that same body.

The information is required before April 18, on which date the "Broadcasting Superintendent" will issue new permits. To date, neither the "Ta Tao" City Government nor the Japanese authorities have interfered with the broadcasts of the various radio stations.

Awkward Position

At the moment, the foreign stations are doing nothing about the matter, pending the receipt of consular advice. The consulates, it is believed, will be placed in an awkward matter, with the exception of the French Consulate. The French radio station "Art and Culture"—not to be confused with PFZ, which only broadcasts meteorological and other such reports in collaboration with Sicca-wei Observatory—has never accepted the jurisdiction of the Chinese authorities. It is registered as a French station, with the French authorities and is situated in the Concession.

The other stations, however, are in a somewhat different position. They are registered with the Ministry of Communications and issued with a permit to operate by that body. But at the same time they have retained a certain amount of independence of action in the matter of times of broadcast and programme material.

It will be recalled that some time ago the Ministry of Communications issued an order that an evening broadcast in English and Chinese from Nanking be relayed by all local radio stations, Chinese and foreign. The former obeyed orders; the latter refused to have their programmes interfered with, fought the matter out—and won in the end, after seeking consular advice.

《字林西报》，
电台
被要求
登记

上海外商电台
将此事提交各自领事馆征求意见。

“我们正在向本国领事馆报告此事，并在决定采取何种行动之前征求他们的意见。”这是上海一些外商无线电公司就一个自称为“广播监理处”的组织致函询问一事所作出的普遍回答。中国电台也收到了这封信，但尚未做出任何决定。

通常，上海的电台在交通部登记；法租界内的电台还需向当地警察当局领取执照。当战事导致上海所有中国政府机关关闭时，这些电台继续运营，尽管其中一些开始怀疑自身的地位。

他们现在收到了这封信，信上没有签名，但盖有该机构的中英文印章。不知其是否为“大道”市政府的下属机构，但其地址列为“哈同大楼316室”。日本新闻检查处也在哈同大楼，位于楼下。

致电台业主的通函要求他们提供过去交通部通常要求的信息，如业主姓名、功率、地点和设备详情，以及播音员姓名，此外还要求提供交通部颁发的许可证副本以及该机构发出的呼号。

这些信息需在4月18日前提供，届时“广播监理”将颁发新许可证。迄今为止，“大道”市政府和日本当局均未干涉各电台的广播。

尴尬处境

目前，外商电台在等待领事建议期间，对此事未采取任何行动。据信，除法国领事馆外，各领事馆将陷入尴尬境地。法国电台“艺术与文化”（Art and Culture）——不要将其与PFZ混淆，后者仅与徐家汇天文台合作广播气象及其他此类报告——从未接受中国当局的管辖。它在法国当局注册为法国电台，位于法租界内。

然而，其他电台的情况略有不同。它们在交通部登记，并由该机构颁发运营许可证。但同时，它们在广播时间和节目内容方面保留了一定的行动独立性。

回想不久前，交通部曾下令，所有本地中外电台必须转播来自南京的中英晚间广播。中方电台服从了命令；外方电台则拒绝让其节目受到干扰，就此展开抗争——在征求领事建议后，最终取得了胜利。

Subject Local Chinese Broadcasting Stations - attitude towards the
so-called "Supervisory Office of Radio Broadcasting Stations"

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by C. Crawford D.Q.

In connection with the instructions issued by the
so-called "Supervisory Office of Radio Broadcasting
Stations," requiring the management of the radio trade
to register with the said office, Room 316, Hardoon
Building, Nanking Road (Vide Special Report dated 11/4/38),
it has been found that none of the chinese broadcasting
stations have complied with this order. Information
has been obtained to the effect that the management of
the Chinese broadcasting stations now operating in the
Settlement and French Concession, will submit joint
petitions, before April 15, to the Settlement and French
Authorities reporting the instructions they have received
from the "Supervisory Office". The management are
of the opinion that their establishments are situated in
the areas under the jurisdiction of the two Municipal
Authorities, and that those functioning in the
International Settlement have assured the Municipal
Police in the form of written guarantees of keeping
their business free from political activities, consequently
they will solicit the advice of the authorities in
connection with the activities of the "Supervisory Office."

Sih Tse Liang
C. D. I.

REPORT
Date......... May 13, 1937.
Subject Censor Board controlling Radio Broadcasting.
Made by ............ and .................... Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang.

A censor board controlling the broadcasting of
programme by Chinese radio stations in Shanghai has been
established in Room 537, 5th floor of the Continental
Emporium Building, Nanking Road.
The Board, with one Li Tz Ler (李子留) as Chief, was
established by the Training Branch of the Central Tangpu of
Nanking, which commenced its functioning in December 1936, and
assisted by delegates from the Ministry of Communications
who has an office in the Telegraph Office, 200 Szechuen Road.
Mr. Li Tz Ler, the Chief censor of Radio Broadcasting,
called at Police Headquarters on May 12 and offered his co-
operation in matters which may come within his jurisdiction.
In the course of a conversation which followed he revealed
that nine radio stations in Shanghai have recently been
ordered to close down for failing to comply with instructions
with Nanking re educational programme. Since he took over
charge, he has been very successful in checking the broadcasting
of songs and stories to stir up ill feeling amongst Chinese
toward foreigners.
There were in the beginning of 1937 thirty-five privately
owned radio broadcasting stations, two Government stations and
five stations run by foreigners. Nine Chinese private
stations have since been closed.

FILE
Superintendent.
D. C. (Special Branch).

该委员会由李子留担任主任，由南京中央党部训练处于1936年12月开始运作的部门建立，并得到交通部代表的协助，交通部在四川路200号电报局设有办公室。
无线电广播首席审查员李子留先生于5月12日造访警察总局，并就其管辖范围内的事项提供合作。在随后的谈话中，他透露，上海有九家电台最近因未遵守南京方面关于教育节目的指示而被勒令关闭。自从他接手负责以来，他在遏制播放煽动中国人对外国人产生恶感的歌曲和故事方面非常成功。
1937年初，共有三十五家私营无线广播电台，两家政府电台和五家由外国人经营的电台。此后，九家中国私营电台已关闭。

Brief Regulations Governing Actions Against Commercial Radio
Broadcasting Stations Which Contravene The Measures For
Directing Broadcasting Programmes, Promulgated by the Ministry
of Communications on April 12, 1937 :-

Article 1. Radio Broadcasting Stations which do
not observe the Measures for Directing the Broadcasting
Programmes of Broadcasting Stations Throughout the Country
shall be dealt with in any of the following three ways:
(1) to be warned, (2) to be ordered to suspend operations,
or (3) to have their licenses withdrawn.

Article 2. A radio broadcasting station may be
warned if it commits any of the following acts:-
(a) Fails to submit various forms and manuscripts for
examination in accordance with regulations after being
notified by the Central Broadcasting Business Direction
Committee.
(b) Fails to observe Section 1 Paragraph 4 of the Measures
for Directing Broadcasting Programmes.
(c) Broadcasts songs and other programmes without first
having obtained approval or permission.
(d) Broadcasts programmes the contents of which differ from
the approved manuscripts.
(e) Fails to observe the directions given by the Central
Broadcasting Business Direction Committee in relation to
broadcasting programmes.

Article 3. A radio broadcasting station may be
ordered to suspend operations for a period of from one to
seven days if it commits any of the following acts:-
(a) Fails to comply with a notice issued in accordance with
Section 1 Paragraph 5 of the Measures for Directing
Broadcasting Programmes or broadcasts amusement programmes
when the National Government has ordered amusements to
be suspended.
pages.zh:
交通部于1937年4月12日颁布的《对违反指导广播节目办法的商业广播电台采取行动之简要规章》：-

第一条. 凡不遵守《全国广播电台指导广播节目办法》的广播电台，应按以下三种方式之一处理：
(1) 警告，(2) 勒令停业，或 (3) 吊销执照。

第二条. 广播电台如有下列行为之一者，可予以警告：-
(a) 经中央广播事业指导委员会通知后，未按规定提交各种表格和稿件供审查。
(b) 不遵守《指导广播节目办法》第一条第四款。
(c) 未经批准或许可擅自播放歌曲及其他节目。
(d) 播出的节目内容与批准的稿件不符。
(e) 不遵守中央广播事业指导委员会关于广播节目的指示。

第三条. 广播电台如有下列行为之一者，可勒令停业一至七天：-
(a) 不遵守根据《指导广播节目办法》第一条第五款发出的通知，或在国民政府下令停止娱乐活动时播放娱乐节目。

pages.en:
-2-
(b) Commits any of the acts mentioned in Article 2 after
having been once warned, or broadcasts any of the
following kinds of programmes without submitting same
for examination and approval:
1) Those which are liable to ruin the traditional
morality of the nation.
2) Those which insult past or present sages and others
who are held in unanimous respect by the people.
3) Mythical stories about devils, gods, ghosts etc.
4) Programmes which contain vulgar or indecent
expressions or which incite wantonness or robbery
etc.
5) Advertisements of contraband goods or publications.
6) Advertisements of drugs, articles or premises
injurious to the body or mind.
7) Programmes which contradict the idea of equality
among peoples and which are liable to give rise to
international bad feelings.
Article 4. A radio broadcasting station may be
ordered to suspend operations for one month or have its
license withdrawn if it broadcast any of the following kinds
of programmes without submitting same for examination and
approval:-
(a) Propaganda being broadcast for a foreign country with
intent to injure the safety of China.
(b) Programmes slandering or contradicting the laws and
orders of the Government.
(c) Programmes slandering or contradicting the principles
of the Kuomintang.
(d) Programmes detrimental to the peace and order of the
society.
Article 5. These Brief Regulations shall be enforced
by the Ministry of Communications.
pages.zh:
-2-
(b) 在被警告一次后仍犯有第二条所述任何行为，或未提交审查批准而播放下列任何类型的节目：
1) 可能破坏国家传统道德的。
2) 侮辱古今圣贤及民众一致尊敬的其他人的。
3) 关于魔鬼、神祇、鬼怪等的神话故事。
4) 包含粗俗或不雅表达，或煽动淫乱、抢劫等的节目。
5) 违禁品或出版物的广告。
6) 损害身心健康的毒品、物品或场所的广告。
7) 违背民族平等理念并可能引起国际不良情绪的节目。
第四条. 广播电台如未提交审查批准而播放下列任何类型的节目，可勒令停业一个月或吊销其执照：-
(a) 以损害中国安全为目的为外国进行的宣传广播。
(b) 诽谤或违背政府法令的节目。
(c) 诽谤或违背国民党原则的节目。
(d) 有害于社会和平秩序的节目。
第五条. 本简要规章由交通部执行。

Standards for Examining the Contents of Broadcasting Programmes,
Promulgated by the Ministry of Communications on April 12, 1937:-
----
All speeches, songs, advertisements and other
programmes to be broadcast from radio broadcasting stations
should be revised or totally prohibited if they correspond
to any of the following descriptions :-
(1) being contradictory to the principles of the Kuomintang.
(2) being injurious to the safety of the nation.
(3) being detrimental to the peace and order of society.
(4) being contradictory to good customs and morality.
(5) being derogatory to past sages and others.
(6) propagating superstition.
(7) containing indecent expressions.
(8) being advertisements for contraband goods or publications.

Hwa Mei Wen Pao dated December 17 :-

GENERAL CHIANG KAI SHEK STOPS PROPOSED BOMBING OF
SIAN BY 400 AEROPLANES

While on his way back to Nanking, on the
night of December 16, Mr. Donald sent a message to Madame
Chiang Kai Shek stating that on his arrival at Sian he
occupied the same residence as the Generalissimo and the
latter instructed him to accompany Mr. T.V. Soong and
General Koo Tsoh Dong to Sian as soon as possible. The
message further stated that Generalissimo Chiang Kai Shek
had given an order stopping the proposed bombing of Sian
by aeroplanes.
General Chiang Ting Wen, one of the high
officers held at Sian, has sent a telegram to Generals
Ho Ying Ching, Liu Shih and Koo Tsoh Dong stating that,
in compliance with an autograph order from the Generalissimo,
he will fly to Loyang on December 17 and that the proposed
bombing must be abandoned.
A serious panic was caused in the City
of Sian by the report that 400 aeroplanes of the Central
Airforce were about to bomb the city.

On the morning of December 17 Mr. Donald
flew from Loyang to Pengpu where he boarded the night train
for Nanking to make a report on his mission. Mr. Donald
will fly to Sian again at 7 a.m. December 17. It is said
that he will remain with the Generalissimo.

On the morning of December 17 the
Central Authorities received a telegram from General Chiang
Ting Wen from Sian stating that he would fly to Loyang
shortly. In the afternoon a telegram was received from
Loyang reporting that General Chiang Ting Wen had arrived
at 11 a.m. by plane. No information was received as to
whether General Chiang Ting Wen had escaped from Sian or had
left with the permission of General Chang Hsueh Liang.
