Shanghai, 27th April, 1938.

Mr. S. Fessenden,
Secretary General,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Shanghai.

Sir,

Re Broadcasting Superintendence in Shanghai

As perhaps you know this office has taken over the superintendence of broadcasting stations and all the affairs connecting with the control and leadership of broadcasting, which have hitherto been under the supervision of the Communications Bureau of the National Government and Central Executive Committee.

Accordingly we sent Notification No.1 dated 20th ult. to all the broadcasting stations in Shanghai stating that above reasons and consequently despatched Notification No.2 dated 31st. ult. again to make the necessary registration to this office for new permits by the 15th inst., but all of them being failed to make this step, the third has been forwarded effecting to cancel their rights of registration unless they make the above procedure on or before the 27th of this month.

In the above circumstances, we are now compelled to ready to stop the business of those, who break the regulations by a some compulsory means, such as to remove or to break down some important parts of machine.

In such case, we are much obliged if you will kindly cooperate with us sending some policemen to let us to attain our object, or at least not to interfere with our purpose.

Yours faithfully,

K. Asano.

Director of Broadcasting
Superintendence Office.

关于上海广播监理事宜

或许您已知悉，本所已接管广播电台的监理工作，以及与此前由国民政府交通部及中央执行委员会监督的广播控制和领导相关的所有事务。

据此，我们于上月20日向上海所有广播电台发出了第1号通知，说明了上述理由，随后又于上月31日再次发出第2号通知，要求各台在本月15日前向本所进行必要登记以换取新许可证，但因各台均未采取此步骤，故已发出第三号通知，规定除非它们在本月27日或之前完成上述程序，否则将取消其注册权利。

在上述情况下，我们现在被迫准备采取某些强制手段，如拆除或破坏机器的重要部件，以停止那些违反规定者的业务。

在此情况下，若您能予以合作，派遣一些警察协助我们实现目标，或者至少不干涉我们的行动，我们将不胜感激。

此致，

K. Asano.

广播监理所
所长。

秘书长今早将此信交给我，并讨论了此事。

Mr. T.K. Ho informs me that the majority of the
owners of Chinese Broadcasting stations, while being
quite willing to register with the Council and give all

附录“F”

助理总监（特别处）。

何德奎（T.K. Ho）先生告诉我，大多数中文广播电台业主虽然完全愿意向工部局注册并提供所需的所有信息，并保证不广播任何政治内容，但他们宁愿停播，也不愿接受日本军方当局或新中国政府当局的许可。

然而，他们会向我们提供所需信息，尽管他们说我们可以转交这些信息，但他们只接受租界当局的管制，不接受其他方面的管制。

Mr. Uyehara,

Shanghai Municipal Police.

Dear Sir,

I beg to express my sincere thanks for
proper measures adopted by the Shanghai Municipal
Council in connection with the suspension of
business of the Dah Ya (大亞) and the Dah Kwong Ming
(大光明) Broadcasting Stations as requested to the
Commissioner of Police through you.

In response to your queries of the 20th
instant on the subject of the operation of new
broadcasting stations, I beg to inform you as follows:

Having been informed of your decision to
reject the applications forwarded to you by the Dah
Lai (大來) and the Wing Sung (永生) Broadcasting
Stations, I have pleasure in taking note of the outcome.

The aforementioned two stations as well
as the Chin Ying (金鷹) Broadcasting Stations registered
with this office prior to the expiration of the date of
registration. Applications for construction had already
been received from them and permits were given accordingly.
The Dah Lai and the Chin Ying Stations reported sometime
ago that they had completed the work. Upon making
technical examination, some defects were found in the
work and they were told to undergo re-examination.
If the work is found satisfactory after re-examination
it is the policy of this office to give them permission
to operate.

尊敬的先生：

谨就通过您向警务总监提出的关于暂停大亞（Dah Ya）和大光明（Dah Kwong Ming）广播电台业务一事，对上海公共租界工部局所采取的适当措施，表示我诚挚的谢意。

针对贵方本月20日就新广播电台运营事宜提出的查询，谨答复如下：

获悉贵方决定驳回转呈给您的大來（Dah Lai）和永生（Wing Sung）广播电台的申请，我对这一结果感到欣慰。

上述两家广播电台以及金鷹（Chin Ying）广播电台均已在注册截止日期前向本办公室注册。本办公室已收到它们的建设申请，并据此颁发了许可证。大來和金鷹广播电台于前段时间报告称工程已完工。经技术检查，发现工程存在一些缺陷，已告知其接受复查。如果复查后工程令人满意，本办公室的政策是向其颁发运营许可。

pages.en:

Apart from the above three stations there are
three more stations, i.e. the "Shanghai" ( 上 海 ),
the "Chin Mei ( 精 美 ) and the "Yang Sz" ( 楊 氏 ),
which have already registered with this office and are
under construction. It is also our policy to give them
permission should they pass the necessary examination.
For the present permits will be issued only to the
above six stations and no further permits will be issued.
If applications be forwarded by the aforementioned
six stations, after having received formal permit from
this office, it is to be hoped that you will make
necessary police inquiries, setting aside technical
examination, and after keeping in touch with me, decide
whether or not to issue permit.

It is matter for regret from the point of view of
controlling the electric wave that the following six
broadcasting stations, i.e. The Sun Sun ( 新 新 ), the
Lee Lee ( 利 利 ), the Tong Lo ( 東 陸 ), the Dah Lo
( 大 陸 ), the Voo Yin( 佛 音 ) and the Hwa Tong( 華 東 ),
which have refused to register with this office, still continue
to operate with your permission only.

It is affirmed that these stations have anti-Japanese
leaning and you are requested to take measures to suspend
broadcasting by these stations on some suitable ground
so as to prevent trouble arising in the future.

Sealed: Asano, Chief of the
Broadcasting Control Office.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

除上述三家广播电台外，另有三家广播电台，即“上海”（Shanghai）、“精美”（Chin Mei）和“楊氏”（Yang Sz），已向本办公室注册并正在建设中。我们的政策也是，若它们通过必要的检查，将向其颁发许可。目前仅向上述六家广播电台颁发许可证，不再颁发其他许可证。如果上述六家广播电台在从本办公室获得正式许可证后提交申请，希望贵方在进行必要的警务调查时，暂不进行技术检查，并在与我保持联系后，决定是否颁发许可证。

从控制电波的角度来看，令人遗憾的是，以下六家广播电台，即新新（The Sun Sun）、利利（Lee Lee）、東陸（Tong Lo）、大陸（Dah Lo）、佛音（Voo Yin）和華東（Hwa Tong），拒绝向本办公室注册，却仅凭贵方的许可继续运营。

据证实，这些电台具有反日倾向，请贵方以适当的理由采取措施暂停这些电台的广播，以防止将来发生麻烦。

盖章：广播管制办公室主任 浅野（Asano）。

pages.en:
(3)
of the Office is anything but to disregard the licensed
rights of the existing stations, as may be clear from the
following explanation of its aim and policy.
(1) The aim of the Broadcast Superintendence Office is to
prevent the confusion of broadcast electric waves in
and around Shanghai, as well as to restrict the broad-
cast items that may disturb peace and order or hamper
the military operation of the Japanese forces. The
Office has no intention of disregarding arbitrarily
the rights already acquired by the existing stations.
It is only for the above-mentioned purposes that the
Office has demanded the registration of the existing
stations therewith.
(2) Neither registration fee nor guarantee money will be
required in any case.
(3) The Office will control the allotment of wave-length,
but will respect the wave-length attributed actually
to the existing stations.
(4) The establishment of a new station requires as a
matter of principle firstly a permission of the Office,
and a permission of the Municipal Council or other
administrative authorities may also be required to
start the broadcast. But the Office will not, in
principle, permit in future the establishment of a
new station, in order to protect the electric waves,
which are already confused, from further confusion.
4. Such being the case, the Municipal Council is
earnestly requested to understand the intention and policy
of the Office, and to take appropriate steps to persuade
the existing radio stations in the Settlement which are not
yet registered with the Office that their rights will best
be protected by placing themselves under the control of the
latter, and induce them to apply for registration as soon
as possible.
pages.zh:
(3)
绝非无视现有电台的持照权利，从其目标和政策的以下解释中可以清楚看出这一点。
(1) 广播监理办公室的目标是防止上海及其周边地区的广播电波混乱，并限制可能扰乱和平与秩序或妨碍日军军事行动的广播内容。该办公室无意任意无视现有电台已经获得的权利。该办公室要求现有电台向其注册，仅是为了上述目的。
(2) 在任何情况下均不收取注册费或保证金。
(3) 该办公室将控制波长分配，但会尊重现有电台实际使用的波长。
(4) 原则上，建立新电台首先需要获得该办公室的许可，开始广播可能还需要获得工部局或其他行政当局的许可。但为了保护已经混乱的电波免受进一步干扰，该办公室原则上将来不会批准建立新电台。
4. 鉴于此，恳请工部局理解该办公室的意图和政策，并采取适当步骤，劝说租界内尚未向该办公室注册的现有无线广播电台，使其认识到置于该办公室的控制之下最能保护其权利，并促使其尽快申请注册。

Promulgated on 15.7.38
Regulations Governing Control of Private
Radio Transmission Stations.
Article 1 Those engaged in broadcasting dialogue and
music by means of radio transmission instrument shall be
known, in general, as radio transmission station (hereafter
abbreviated as broadcasting station) and the installation
and operation of such stations are to be subject to the
control of these regulations.
Article 2 Any person who is desirous of establishing a
broadcasting station shall first submit an application to
the Radio Transmission Control Office (hereafter to be
referred to as Control Office).
Article 3 The licensee of the broadcasting station shall
furnish the following particulars in the application:
(1) Name of the society or organization, nature of the
organization, address and the name of the licensee.
(2) The object of the establishment of a broadcasting
station.
(3) Name of the broadcasting station, its organization
and its general budgetary statement.
(4) Detailed statement regarding the mechanical construction
and installation of the broadcasting machine to be accompanied
by illustrations.
(5) Location of the broadcasting station and the studio.
Article 4 In the event of the application being approved,
the Control Office shall issue a permit for the installation
work to be commenced. No installation work shall be
undertaken by the broadcasting station until the receipt
of the permit.
Article 5 The permit for installation work shall be
valid for 2 months from the date of issue, however, should
the applicant wish to apply for an extension due to some
special circumstances, an additional one month's extension

J
副本
颁布于1938年7月15日
私人无线电发射台管制条例。
第一条 凡利用无线电发射仪器从事对话和音乐广播者，统称为无线电发射台（以下简称广播电台），此类电台的安装和运营须受本条例管制。
第二条 任何欲建立广播电台者，应首先向无线电发射管制办公室（以下简称管制办公室）提交申请。
第三条 广播电台持照人应在申请书中提供以下详情：
(1) 社团或组织名称、组织性质、地址及持照人姓名。
(2) 建立广播电台的目的。
(3) 广播电台名称、组织结构及总体预算说明。
(4) 广播机器的机械构造和安装的详细说明，并附插图。
(5) 广播电台及演播室的位置。
第四条 如申请获准，管制办公室应颁发许可证，方可开始安装工程。广播电台在收到许可证之前，不得进行任何安装工程。
第五条 安装许可证自签发之日起有效期为2个月，但是，如果申请人因特殊情况希望申请延期，只要在第一份许可证到期前不迟于两周提交此类申请，可再给予一个月的延期

pages.en:
(2)
shall be granted provided that such application is submitted
not later than two weeks before the expiry of the first
permit.
Article 6 On completion of the installation work, the
machinery as well as the general construction work will be
subjected to minute examination by an officer of the Control
Office and should it be found to be up to the required
standard, broadcasting permit will be issued in exchange
for the installation permit.
Article 7 No broadcasting, except during the specified
hour, shall be indulged in by the station prior to the
issue of the full broadcasting permit. The adjustment of
the relay transmission apparatus shall be made with the
aid of "sham" aerial.
Article 8 The broadcasting permit shall be valid for one
year, but subject to renewal within one month before the
expiry of the period. Renewal applications will be
examined by the Control Office and the renewal will be
effected provided that everything is in order.
Article 9 Once the broadcasting permit is issued, no
station shall alter its name, address or the address
of the studio.
Article 10 The permit is not transferable.
Article 11 The call signal will be designated by the
Control Office.
Article 12 The carrier frequency will be allocated by
the Control Office.
Article 13 The power of the wave will be specified by the
Control Office.
Article 14 The broadcasting machine shall invariably be
those fitted with the crystal point control system.
Article 15 Those stations using high power waves shall
restrict the power as much as possible so as not to
interfere with the operations of other stations. In the
event of the wireless wave being found to be too powerful

Article 16 All broadcasting stations shall announce
briefly their call signal, and the carrier frequency at an
interval of approximately 30 minutes.
Article 17 All radio commentators and technicians shall
have qualifications stipulated by the Control Office.
Article 18 Functions of a broadcasting station shall
be limited to the following items. The programme, however,
shall be subject to modification or restriction at the
discretion of the Control Office.
(1) Lectures and other addresses beneficial to the general
public.
(2) News Item.
(3) Music, play, entertainment, etc.
(4) Commercial advertisement.
Article 19 The Control Office shall have access, at all
time, to all the books kept by the broadcasting stations
and shall also inspect the installation when necessary.
Any report or documents called for by the Control Office
shall be forwarded by the management.
Article 20 The broadcasting station shall abide by the
following stipulations set forth by the Control Office;
(1) That no station shall resort to such act calculated
to disturb the business of other stations.
(2) That no station shall broadcast or disseminate
news or reports lacking confirmation.
(3) That no station shall exceed the limit of advertise-
ment requirements and unnecessarily engage in dispatching
message or signal to specified listeners.
(4) That no station shall broadcast speech, report,
play or news that are likely to disturb peace and order
and traditional good customs.

第二十条 广播电台应遵守管制局制定的下列规定；
(1) 任何电台不得采取旨在干扰其他电台业务的行为。
(2) 任何电台不得广播或传播未经证实的新闻或报道。
(3) 任何电台不得超过广告要求的限度，并无必要地向特定听众发送信息或信号。
(4) 任何电台不得广播可能扰乱和平秩序及传统良俗的演讲、报道、戏剧或新闻。

Radio Broadcast Control Administration
November 30, 1938.
Police Department,
S. M. C.
Dear Sirs,
Re Disposal of Unregistered Radio Stations
Ever since the establishment of this administration
in March this year, five radio stations, namely, Hwa Tung
(華東), Dah Loh (大陸), Tung Fong (東方), Foh Ing
(佛音), and Sun Sun (秀々), operating in the Inter-
national Settlement, have been warned time and again to
effect registration with this office.
In spite of these warnings, however, the stations
in question continue to broadcast. Such an action on
the part of these stations are not only detrimental to
the prestige of this administration, but also tends to
disrupt the system of control over the wave length and
in view of these circumstances, final letters of warning
were addressed to the stations concerned on November 5
this year in an attempt to bring about reflection on their
mistaken attitude, but without avail.
As no sign of repentance has been forthcoming, we
have now struck off their names from the list acting on
the assumption that these stations have automatically
forfeited the right of broadcasting enjoyed under legally
established control by their refusal to acknowledge this
system.
The carrier frequencies formerly assumed by these
delinquent stations have already been granted by us to
certain Japanese and foreign radio stations duly registered
with this administration and we take this opportunity to
apprise you of these changes for your information.
Yours faithfully,
(Sgd) Kazuwo Asano,
Superintendent.

1938年11月30日。
致：
上海公共租界工部局警务处，
敬启者：
关于处置未注册广播电台事宜
自今年三月本局成立以来，已在公共租界内运营的五家广播电台，即华东（Hwa Tung）、大陆（Dah Loh）、东方（Tung Fong）、佛音（Foh Ing）和秀々（Sun Sun），已被多次警告向本局办理注册。
尽管有此等警告，有关电台仍继续广播。这些电台的此类行为不仅损害了本局的威信，而且倾向于破坏波长管制体系。鉴于此等情况，本局于今年11月5日向有关电台发出了最后警告信，试图促使其反思其错误态度，但未见成效。
由于未见悔意迹象，我们现在将其名称从名单中除名，基于这样的假设：这些电台因拒绝承认这一体系，已自动丧失了在法律建立的管制下享有的广播权。
这些违规电台原先占用的载波频率已由我们授予某些已向本局正式注册的日本及外国广播电台，我们借此机会告知你们这些变更，以供参考。
此致，
（签名）浅野一夫（Kazuwo Asano），
督察长。

May 8, 1938.

MAINICHI

"S.M.C.'S ATTITUDE IN THE MATTER OF BROADCASTING
CONTROL"

The Shanghai Mainichi publishes the
following leading article under the above heading:-

It is only natural that control of
broadcasting stations in Shanghai should be exercised by the
Japanese army after it had saved the Foreign Settlements
from war destruction. The rebuilding of a greater Shanghai
by the Japanese army is making rapid progress. As
military operations are still going on near Hsuchow □□□
and along the Chientang River, any activities which are
liable to obstruct war operations cannot be permitted in
Shanghai which lies within the area occupied by the Japanese
army. Since the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities,
the Japanese navy has blockaded the China sea coast for a
length of 300 miles. The Chinese people are trying
every kind of propaganda to win the sympathy of the neutral
Powers, to prevent dissension among the people and to
suppress any anti-Chiang Kai-shek movement. They are
continuing to conduct such propaganda under the names of
neutrals. It is a matter of great importance and the
Japanese army must put an end to such activities. The
control of broadcasting has an important bearing to military
affairs. The air in the area occupied by the Japanese
army does not belong to any foreign concession;it belongs
to China, therefore, it is only reasonable that the Japanese
army should exercise control over it.

After the Greater Shanghai
Broadcasting Control Office had received on March 20

“工部局在广播管制问题上的态度”

《上海每日新闻》以上述标题发表以下社论：

既然日军将外国租界从战争破坏中拯救出来，由日军对上海的广播电台实施管制是自然而然的。日军建设大上海的工作正在迅速推进。由于徐州□□□附近及钱塘江沿岸的军事行动仍在进行，任何可能妨碍作战的行动在上海这个位于日军占领区内的城市都是不被允许的。自中日敌对行动爆发以来，日本海军已封锁了中国海岸线长达300英里。中国人正尝试各种宣传手段，以赢得中立国家的同情，防止民众内部出现分歧，并镇压任何反蒋介石运动。他们继续以中立者的名义进行此类宣传。这是一件极其重要的事情，日军必须终止此类活动。广播管制与军事事务有着重要的关联。日军占领区的空域不属于任何外国租界；它属于中国，因此，由日军对其实施管制是合乎情理的。

The reason why the Greater

It was difficult to receive the broadcasting with the

Stations Are Waiting
For Settlement By
S.M.C. Now

Despite the fact that yesterday
was considered by the Broadcast-
ing Stations Supervising Bureau as
the last day, for registration of
Chinese broadcasting stations in
Shanghai, several Chinese stations
continued their broadcasts without
registration, while others suspend-

notices served to them on Wednes-
day.

The matter was still unsettled
and despite the fact than the Japan-
ese had reportedly threatened to
take "determined action" in case
of non-registration, no disturbances
were reported.

Those stations which suspended
broadcasts appeared to be waiting
for the results of negotiations be-
tween the Japanese-supported
Bureau and authorities of the
Shanghai Municipal Council. It
was reported, however, that a re-
presentative of the Bureau had seen
Mr. Stirling Fessenden, General
Secretary of the Council, on the
question but no agreement was
reached. The Japanese became im-
patient and served the deadline
notices.

It would appear that most of the
suspended stations are adopting a
wait-and-see attitude hoping the
Council will reach an agreement
whereby the stations would register
with the Council: Interviewed, an
officer of a big broadcasting station
said that his station had decided to
close unless otherwise ordered by
the Council.

While the question was still un-
settled, a new Chinese broadcast-
ing station, the "Ta Kwang Ming

广播事宜
仍在讨论中

各电台正等待
工部局目前
作出解决

尽管昨天被广播电台监理局视为上海中国广播电台注册的最后一天，但仍有几家中国电台在未注册的情况下继续广播，而其他电台则暂停营业，无视周三向其送达的通知。

此事仍未解决，尽管据报道日本方面威胁称，如果不注册将采取“坚决行动”，但未报告发生任何骚乱。

那些暂停广播的电台似乎在等待日本支持的监理局与上海公共租界工部局当局之间谈判的结果。然而，据报道，监理局代表曾就此事会见工部局总秘书斯特林·费森登先生，但未达成协议。日本方面变得不耐烦，并发出了最后期限通知。

看来大多数停播电台都采取观望态度，希望工部局能达成一项协议，使电台向工部局注册：在接受采访时，一家大型广播电台的一名官员表示，除非工部局另有命令，否则他的电台决定关闭。

就在问题尚未解决之际，一家新的中国广播电台“大光明广播电台”于昨天中午正式成立。

forcibly compelled to register with
the Bureau. It was also agreed
that the stations would not be re-
quired to register with the Council,
but that the latter would under-
take to see that the stations did
not broadcast anti-Japanese pro-
paganda nor anything which would
tend to disturb the peace and good
order of the Settlement. As part
of its responsibility for the main-
tenance of peace and order within
its jurisdiction, the Council under-
took to close any station which did
not comply with Council require-
ments or disobeyed the order re-
garding preservation of peace.

It was learnt from S.M.C. officials
yesterday that agreement along the
above lines had been reached fol-
lowing recent negotiations. It was
stated also that the Chinese stations
had agreed to submit their pro-
grammes to Council officials for ap-
proval before broadcasting.

There are 23 Chinese stations
functioning in Shanghai at the pre-
sent time and practically all of
these suspended operations on April
28 when threatened with closure
and confiscation of equipment if
they failed to register with the Ja-
panese-controlled Bureau. Some of
the stations opened later, but it was
not until yesterday that the major-
ity were again on the air.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL - 7 MAY 1938 SPEC）

日方未对
各电台
施压

经磋商后
本地中文广播
机构恢复运营

工部局承担
责任

将审查具有反日
及煽动恐慌性质
的宣传

在得到不会强行迫使上海中文广播电台向广播台监理局登记的保证后，本地中文广播电台于昨日恢复了常规节目，这些电台此前已停业相当长一段时间。

本地大多数中文电台停播广播节目，严重干扰了广告合同的履行，并对华人社区造成了一些不便。尽管早些时候有威胁称若不向该局登记将被强行关闭，但一些小型电台仍继续运营，而23家中文电台中的大多数则选择了停业。

上海公共租界工部局与由日本人控制的监理局当局进行了半官方谈判，结果是后者作出保证，不会强行迫使中文电台向该局登记。双方还达成协议，不要求这些电台向工部局登记，但工部局将负责确保各电台不播放反日宣传或任何可能扰乱租界和平与良好秩序的内容。作为在其管辖范围内维持和平与秩序的责任的一部分，工部局承诺关闭任何不符合工部局要求或违抗有关维持和平命令的电台。

据工部局官员昨日透露，经过最近的谈判，已达成上述方针的协议。另据悉，中文电台已同意在广播前将其节目提交工部局官员审批。

目前上海共有23家中文电台在运作，实际上所有这些电台都在4月28日暂停了运营，当时它们受到威胁，若不在日本控制的监理局登记，将面临关闭和设备没收。部分电台随后重新开播，但直到昨日，大多数电台才再次恢复广播。

（印：上海公共租界工部局 - 1938年5月7日 特急）

pages.en:
Broadcasting
Dispute Here
Said Settled

A satisfactory settlement of
the question of registration of
local Chinese broadcasting sta-
tions has been reached as a
result of the negotiations made
with the Japanese authorities by
the Shanghai Municipal Council.
The settlement is in the form
of an informal understanding
whereby the Japanese authori-
ties have agreed that they will
not forcefully compel the re-
gistration of broadcasting sta-
tions. In other words, registra-
tion of the broadcasters will be
a voluntary matter.
At the same time, the Council,
which was originally asked by
the station owners to take up
the registration, will also re-
frain from proceeding on the
matter.
The station owners, however,
have been warned by Settlement
police authorities to keep off the
air any program of an anti-
Japanese nature. They are given
to understand that if this warn-
ing is observed the question of
registration will be held in abey-
ance.
Station owners were holding a
meeting yesterday evening re-
garding the date on which they
will resume broadcasting, which
they suspended more than a
week ago when they refused to
comply with the registration pro-
cedure. It was tentatively plan-
ned that operations will be re-
sumed on Tuesday, May 10.
pages.zh:
本地广播
争议据称
已解决

通过与日本当局的谈判，上海公共租界工部局就本地中文广播电台登记问题达成了令人满意的解决方案。该解决方案采取非正式谅解的形式，据此，日本当局同意不会强行迫使广播电台进行登记。换言之，广播机构的登记将是自愿性质的。

与此同时，最初应电台业主请求介入登记事宜的工部局，也将不再就此事项采取行动。

然而，租界警务当局已警告电台业主，不得播出任何具有反日性质的节目。据告知，若遵守此警告，登记问题将暂缓处理。

电台业主于昨晚举行会议，商讨恢复广播的日期，他们因拒绝遵守登记程序而于一周多前停止了广播。初步计划于5月10日（星期二）恢复运营。

April 21. 1938.
Afternoon Translation.

Hua Mei Chen Pao :-

JAPANESE AND RADIO COMMUNICATIONS

According to reliable information from
foreign sources, the local Japanese military authorities
are working strenuously to accelerate the development
of wireless communications so as to introduce radio
communication with San Francisco, U.S.A. As the Chinese
radio stations at Chenju and Liuhang have been destroyed,
they are constructing two new radio stations in Shanghai:
one at Yangtsepoo and the other at Kiangwan.
All materials and technical experts required
for the construction of these two stations have been
sent here from Tokyo. This work is being undertaken by
the local Japanese military authorities because the
Chinese Government has established a radio station in
Hankow to communicate with the Philippine Islands.
pages.zh:
1938年4月21日。
下午译稿。

《华美晚报》：

日方与无线电通讯

据来自外国的可靠消息，本地日本军事当局正努力加速发展无线通讯，以便开通与美国旧金山的无线电通信。由于陈菊（音译）和六行（音译）的中国电台已被摧毁，他们正在上海建造两座新电台：一座位于杨树浦，另一座位于江湾。

建造这两座电台所需的所有材料和技术专家均已从东京运抵此地。此项工作由本地日本军事当局承担，因为中国政府已在汉口设立了一座电台，用于与菲律宾群岛进行通信。

April 16, 1938. Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition and other local newspapers:

JAPANESE AND RADIO STATIONS

With reference to the order of the Radio
Broadcasting Station Control Office to local broadcasting
stations to register with the Office before April 15, it

have decided to refuse to register. It is not known

1938年4月16日。上午译稿。

《大美晚报》晨版及其他本地报纸：

日方与广播电台

关于无线电广播台监理办公室命令本地广播电台在4月15日前向该办公室登记一事，现获悉本地外国广播电台已决定拒绝登记。尚不清楚监理办公室是否会采取严厉措施对付这些外国广播电台。后者已针对手榴弹袭击采取了预防措施。

法租界当局否认日本报纸所称的不合作指控。公共租界当局也否认了有关他们已命令广播电台遵守广播台监理办公室的命令并向其登记的报道。

April 15, 1938. Morning Translation.

China Daily News and other local newspapers:

JAPANESE AND RADIO STATIONS

The Shanghai Radio Broadcasting Station Control
Office, established by the Japanese authorities, is
exercising control over local broadcasting stations and
so far, no trouble has taken place.
However, most of the broadcasting stations in
the French Concession have not yet submitted to Japanese
supervision, because the authorities of the French
Concession do not recognize the authority of the Radio
Broadcasting Station Control Office and have strictly
instructed all broadcasting stations in the Concession not

pages.zh:
1938年4月15日。上午译稿。

《中国日报》及其他本地报纸：

日方与广播电台

由日本当局设立的上海无线电广播台监理办公室正在对本地广播电台实施控制，截至目前，未发生任何纠纷。

然而，法租界内的大多数广播电台尚未服从日本监管，因为法租界当局不承认无线电广播台监理办公室的权威，并严令租界内所有广播电台不得服从监理办公室的监管。日本当局对此极为愤怒，正计划采取有效措施处理此事。

pages.en:

Morning Translation.

JAPANESE AND RADIO STATIONS

pages.zh:
1938年4月14日。
上午译稿。

日方与广播电台

现获悉，法租界当局拒绝承认该组织为有权监督或控制法租界内无线电广播电台的合法机构。

pages.en:

CONTROL OF BROADCASTING IN SHANGHAI

ordering them to fill in a form and register with the Office

上海广播管制

On April 1 the Radio Broadcasting Control

pages.zh:
1938年4月2日。上午译稿。

日方掌控广播

4月1日，由日本当局在哈同大楼220室组建的无线电广播监理办公室接管了原由交通部和中国国民党中央宣传部处理的无线电广播控制权。

pages.en:
948
Nippon Radio Control
Fought; S'hai Chinese
Broadcasts Suspended

STATIONS REJECT
JAPANESE ORDER
OF REGISTRATION

D. 68/3/6

Desired Information Sent SMC, Direct Dealings
With Nippon Organ Avoided; Threats Made
To Forcibly End Chinese Broadcasts

SMC NEGOTIATING DISPUTE

All but three Chinese radio stations in Shanghai suspended operations voluntarily today rather than comply with the Japanese request that they register with the Broadcasting Superintendent's Office in the Hardoon Building. The deadline for registration was reached yesterday when officials of all stations held a meeting and decided to go off the air temporarily until a satisfactory solution of the present impasse had been reached.

One possible reason for the suspension is the reported threat of the Japanese that unless their order was obeyed before today, when the last of three notifications expired, they would remove part of the machinery of Chinese stations within the Settlement to prevent further broadcasting.

Chinese Standpoint
The standpoint of the Chinese stations is that while willing to supply the desired information, they will not supply it to the Japanese direct, preferring to deal with the Settlement authorities. In keeping with this policy, Settlement authorities this morning received registration blanks carrying all desired information.

The Broadcasting Superintendent's Office, however, refuses to be satisfied since refusal to register with the office direct implies non-recognition of its existence or right of censorship.

S.M.C. Negotiating
Settlement authorities are at present negotiating with the Japanese office on the subject in an effort to reach an agreement. Any attempt on the part of Nipponese consular police or military to remove machinery from the stations would be viewed in a serious light, it is understood, since the stations are private property. Foreign stations which also received notifications requesting them to register have paid no heed to them and it is understood that they are not being molested, the Japanese apparently wishing to settle the problem of control of Chinese stations before tackling the more difficult problem of compelling foreign obedience.

Desired Information
The desired information, originally requested before April 18, is as follows:
1.—The name of the proprietor or group of owners, nationality, age, place of residence and other pertinent information.
2.—The purpose of the station's operation.
3.—The financial status of the station and the source of revenue.
4.—Power, location and detailed plans of the transmitting equipment.
5.—Location of the studio.
6.—Call signal.
7.—Frequency of the transmitter.
8.—Names of announcers and engineers, their nationality, age, place of residence and salary.
9.—A copy of the permit, if any issued by the Ministry of Communications.

According to the notifications, the offices of the "Broadcasting superintendent's Office" is in the Hardoon Building, Room 316.

Test Case?
At the meeting held yesterday it was decided that stations could operate or suspend as they chose, the three which continued operating possibly intending to act as a test case. If the threat to force suspension by removing part of the machinery is carried out, it is expected that these stations will be off the air by tonight.

If the Japanese win their fight to control Chinese-owned stations an increase in the number of foreign-owned stations is expected to result. At present foreign stations broadcast Chinese news programs the control of which is the real objective of the Japanese action.

When Chinese newspapers fell under Japanese censorship, most of them suspended, being replaced by foreign-controlled newspapers which ignored censorship requests. This may now also result in the radio field.

（批：DCSB / 28/4 / Like / Q工）
pages.zh:
948
日本无线电管制
发生冲突；上海华方
广播暂停

各电台拒绝
日本的注册令

D. 68/3/6

所需情报已送交工部局，避免与日方机构直接打交道；日方威胁要强行终止华方广播

工部局正在就争端进行谈判

上海除三家中文广播电台外，其余均于今日自愿停止运营，以免遵从日方要求向位于哈同大楼（Hardoon Building）的广播监理处注册。注册的截止日期是昨日，当时各电台负责人举行会议，决定暂时停播，直至目前的僵局得到令人满意的解决。

停播的一个可能原因是据传日方发出威胁：除非在最后一份通知到期的今日之前服从其命令，否则他们将拆除租界内华方电台的部分设备，以阻止进一步广播。

中方立场
中方电台的立场是，虽然愿意提供所需情报，但不会直接向日方提供，而是倾向于与租界当局打交道。本着这一政策，租界当局今晨收到了载有所有所需情报的注册空白表格。

然而，广播监理处拒绝接受这一做法，因为拒绝直接向该处注册意味着不承认其存在或审查权。

工部局进行谈判
租界当局目前正就此问题与日方机构进行谈判，以期达成协议。据悉，如果日本领事警察或军方试图从电台移除设备，将被视为严重事件，因为这些电台属于私有财产。同样收到要求注册通知的外国电台未予理会，据悉它们并未受到骚扰，日方显然希望在着手解决更困难的外国服从问题之前，先解决对华方电台的控制问题。

所需情报
最初于4月18日之前要求提供的情报如下：
1.—业主或所有者团体的姓名、国籍、年龄、居住地及其他相关情报。
2.—电台运营的目的。
3.—电台的财务状况及收入来源。
4.—发射设备的功率、位置及详细图纸。
5.—演播室的位置。
6.—呼号。
7.—发射频率。
8.—播音员和工程师的姓名、国籍、年龄、居住地及薪水。
9.—交通部颁发的许可证副本（如有）。

根据通知，“广播监理处”的办公室位于哈同大楼316室。

测试案例？
在昨日举行的会议上，决定各电台可自行选择运营或停播，继续运营的三家可能打算作为测试案例。如果通过移除部分设备来强行停播的威胁得以实施，预计这些电台将在今晚前停播。

如果日方在控制华人拥有的电台方面获胜，预计外国拥有的电台数量将会增加。目前，外国电台播放中文新闻节目，而控制这些节目才是日方行动的真正目标。

当中文报纸落入日本审查之下时，大多数报纸停刊，取而代之的是无视审查要求的外国控制报纸。这种情况现在也可能在无线电领域出现。

（批：DCSB / 28/4 / Like / Q工）

Radio Broadcasting
Stations Function;

About 10 Chinese radio stations
were functioning about as usual
today, despite the fact that yes-
terday was their deadline for

无线电广播
电台运作；
未报告发生麻烦

尽管昨日是上海约10家中文广播电台向日方注册的截止日期，且它们并未注册，但这些电台今日仍大致照常运作。虽然工部局昨晚听取了主席关于谈判情况的报告，但工部局与日本当局之间今日尚未就此事项达成任何安排。

日方不太可能采取强制措施迫使电台服从。目前认为，一项临时安排已接近达成，即电台既不向日方也不向工部局注册，但它们已被警告，空中出现反日宣传可能导致其被关闭。特别是那些播放新闻的电台将受到日方监视，以确保其节目和评论不致失控。

其他因拒绝遵向日方要求而已关闭的电台仍在观望，等待结果明朗后再恢复营业。

Fail To Register

radio broadcasting stations in

316, Hardoon Building. Neither

外国电台
未注册

无线电注册期限已过；
未采取强制服从行动

上海广播电台的注册期限于今日届满，没有任何一家外国电台遵从位于哈同大楼316室的自称“广播监理处”的情报索取要求。该组织也未采取任何步骤强制执行其“要求”，这些要求首次公开于上周日的《上海晚邮报》（Shanghai Evening Post）版面上。
由于该组织未表明其是否具有官方地位，促使各国领事和电台采取观望态度，迄今为止唯一的结果是一家电台周围的窗户被装上屏蔽物，以防可能的投掷手榴弹。
该函件要求在4月15日前注册，并提供有关电台、员工、业主、设备、财务的详细情报以及交通部许可证的副本。
与此同时，法租界当局和工部局否认了《上海日报》（Shanghai Nippo）昨日刊文中的说法。该报声称，租界当局（与工部局采取的态度相反）已告知中文广播电台“不要理会日本关于广播管制的通知”。
与此同时，工部局否认曾告知租界内的中文电台“它们将由任何取代中央政府交通部本地办事处的机构进行监管”。
《上海日报》称：“令人深感遗憾的是，面对日本当局希望改善中文广播……等愿望，租界当局采取了如此不妥协的态度。” 截至目前，无线电局势处于僵持状态。

（批：2 14/4）
（批：Q 16/4）

Radio Stations
Await Further
Developments

Earlier reports that local Chinese
and foreign-owned radio stations
will let matters stand as they are
until the "Radio Superintendent's
Office" of obscure identity takes a

Following deliberations upon re-

From what could be learned yes-

Strange though it may seem, the

Stations in the French Conces-

广播电台
等待进一步
事态发展
领事馆、警方称
此阶段评论多余

此前有关本地华资和外资产广播电台将维持现状，直到身份不明的“无线电监理处”采取更明确态度的报道，于昨日在此得到证实。
周五收到“无线电监理处”两份通知后，经过审议，第一份宣布该局存在，第二份要求提供电台及其各自运营情况的详细信息，上海的广播演播室要么求助于警方，要么求助于各自的领事官员。
据昨日了解，领事和警方当局均 refrain from（克制）对局势发表评论，因为认为在此阶段对其可能态度的声明纯属假设且多余。
尽管看似奇怪，但这个显然试图对本地广播单位实行管制的新机构的身份尚不明确。据报道，通知未署名，但盖有该局的中英文印章。
据悉，法租界内的电台持有法国警方颁发的执照，已向这些当局寻求建议，而公共租界的演播室则尽可能向其各自的领事馆求助。
回顾一下，尽管在上海被日军包围之前，市内外国电台是在交通部许可证下运营的，但它们保留了选择自身节目内容的特权。

（批：S! 13/4）

pages.en:
Japanese Angered
Over Radios

French Concession Stand
Refusing Permission for
Interference Resented

Japanese official quarters were reported yesterday by the "Shanghai Nippo" to be "displeased" by the adamant refusal of the French Concession authorities to allow Japanese control over Chinese radio broadcasting stations.

The French stand, the daily declared, was in sharp contrast to the attitude assumed by the Shanghai Municipal Council, which informed Chinese stations in the Settlement that they would be supervised by any organ that replaces the local office of the Nationalist Ministry of Communications.

The Council, however, retained full control over the actual operations of these stations, the journal added.

Need Not Pay Attention

Chinese broadcasting stations in the Concession, on the other hand, were alleged to have been informed by the authorities that they need not pay any attention to the Japanese notices on the control of broadcasting.

Moreover, the journal declared, the owners of the Chinese broadcasting stations were informed by the Concession authorities that the latter were opposed to any contact between these stations and the Japanese control organ.

"It is deeply to be regretted," the "Nippo" said, "that the Concession authorities have adopted such an uncompromising attitude, in the face of the Japanese authorities' desire to brighten up Chinese broadcasts and to maintain peace and order in the occupied areas."

Only about 24 stations are in operation in Shanghai now, as contrasted with about 40 before the outbreak of the hostilities, the daily reported.
pages.zh:
日方因无线电
问题感到愤怒

法租界立场
拒绝允许干涉引发不满

据《上海日报》昨日报道，日本官方人士对法租界当局坚决拒绝允许日本控制中文广播电台表示“不满”。

该日报宣称，法方的立场与工部局采取的态度形成鲜明对比，工部局告知租界内的中文电台，它们将由任何取代国民政府交通部本地办事处的机构进行监管。

该报补充说，然而，工部局保留了对这些电台实际运营的完全控制权。

无需理会

另一方面，据称租界内的中文广播电台已被告知，无需理会日本关于广播管制的通知。

此外，该报宣称，中文广播电台的业主已被告知，法租界当局反对这些电台与日本管制机构进行任何接触。

《上海日报》称：“令人深感遗憾的是，面对日本当局希望改善中文广播并在占领区维持和平与秩序的愿望，租界当局采取了如此不妥协的态度。”

该日报报道，目前上海仅有约24家电台在运营，而在敌对行动爆发前约有40家。

pages.en:
540

French, S.M.C. Officials
Deny Shanghai Nippo
Story On Radio Issue

Both French Concession authorities and the Shanghai Municipal Council yesterday denied reports appearing in a Shanghai Nippo article of yesterday's issue commenting upon their respective attitudes on the question of Japanese control over Chinese radio broadcasting stations.

In its article, the Shanghai Nippo reported that Japanese official quarters were "displeased by the adamant refusal of the French Concession authorities to allow Japanese control over Chinese radio broadcasting stations."

The French stand, it was alleged by the report, was in sharp contrast to the attitude assumed by the Shanghai Municipal Council, "which informed Chinese stations in the Settlement that they would be supervised by any organ replacing the local office of the Central Government's Ministry of Communications." The Council, however, retained full control over the actual operations of these stations, the journal added.

On behalf of the S.M.C., a spokesman yesterday denied the Nippo's assertion that Chinese radio stations in the Settlement were so informed by the Council. French Concession authorities also denied the report that "Chinese broadcasting stations in the Concession were informed that they need not pay any attention to the Japanese notices on the control of broadcasting," and that "Chinese owners of stations were informed that the Concession authorities were opposed to any contact between these stations and the Japanese control organ."

Continuing, the Nippo declared that "it is deeply to be regretted that the Concession authorities have adopted such an uncompromising attitude in the face of the Japanese authorities' desire to brighten up Chinese broadcasts and to maintain peace and order in the occupied areas."

法租界当局和上海公共租界工部局昨日均否认了昨日一期《上海日报》（Shanghai Nippo）文章中的报道，该文章评论了各方在日本控制中国广播电台问题上的各自态度。

《上海日报》在其文章中报道称，日本官方人士对“法租界当局坚决拒绝允许日本控制中国广播电台”感到“不悦”。

据报道声称，法国的立场与上海公共租界工部局所采取的态度形成鲜明对比，后者“通知租界内的中国电台，它们将受任何取代中央政府交通部本地办事机构的机关监督”。该报还补充说，然而，工部局保留了对这些电台实际运营的完全控制权。

工部局一名发言人昨日代表工部局否认了《上海日报》关于工部局曾如此通知租界内中国电台的说法。法租界当局也否认了有关“租界内的中国广播电台被告知无需理会日本关于控制广播的通知”以及“电台的中国业主被告知租界当局反对这些电台与日本控制机构进行任何接触”的报道。

《上海日报》接着宣称，“令人深感遗憾的是，面对日本当局希望改善中国广播并在占领区维持和平与秩序的愿望，租界当局采取了如此毫不妥协的态度。”

No Agreement
Reached Here
On Broadcasts
Council Meeting Today

CHINESE STILL
STAYING ON AIR
Ultimatum On Deadline
Received By Stations;
Action Unlikely

With the Japanese deadline
reached today for all Chinese
broadcasting stations in Shanghai
to register with the Broadcasting
Station Supervision Bureau in the
Hardoon Building, the Shanghai
Municipal Council was meeting at
the Administration Building this
afternoon. At this meeting Coun-
cillors were to hear a report by
Mr. C. S. Franklin, chairman, on

Station XMHC, known as the
Overseas Broadcasting Company
on Avenue Road, received a notice
yesterday, dated May 3, and sign-
ed Major K. Asano, director of
Broadcasting Superintendent's Of-
fice, ordering it to suspend busi-
ness. The proprietors of XMHC
are Chinese of American citizen-
ship and declare that their station
is registered as an American con-
cern at the American Consulate.
The order reads: "Having fail-
ed to observe the advice circulated
in note number 3 dated March 28,
1938, your station is hereby strict-
ly requested to suspend broadcast-
ing further."

the results or progress of negotia-
tions he has been carrying on re-
cently with Japanese authorities
to settle the knotty problem.
Meanwhile, however, it was not
believed today that any definite
agreement had been reached
on the matter Reports insert from
various quarters differed, but it
appeared that while no accord had
been yet found, it was unlikely
that the Japanese would take any
immediate steps to stop broad-
casts forcibly if the requirements
were not fulfilled.
Half Suspended
Of approximately 20 larger Chi-
nese broadcasting studios, half of
them have already suspended
operations, rather than submit to
Japanese control. Of the remain-
ing 10, one is a Chinese Christian
establishment broadcasting re-
ligious matter. The other nine
continue to broadcast, but only
one is known to have a Japan-
ese permit. The majority are
located in the western part of the
Settlement.
In some well-informed foreign

under conditions approved by the

anti-Japanese matter must be de-

other quarters, however it was
held very unlikely that
any such agreement
had been reached. Japanese un-

Still Broadcasting
A Chinese report today stated
that unregistered stations are
broadcasting as usual today, and
are determined not to register
with the Japanese Radio Super-
intendent Office, adding that these
stations would rather suspend
business.
Most stations stopped work
about a week ago, though a few
resumed operations a few days
later. The Japanese threatened
at that time that unless their
order was obeyed, they would re-
move part of the machinery of
Chinese stations within the
Settlement to prevent further
broadcasting. The Chinese sta-
tions were willing to supply the

Any attempt on the part of the

此处未就
广播问题
达成协议
今日召开
工部局会议
听取会谈
报告
中国人仍
在播音
最后通牒期限
已至各电台；
不太可能采取行动

随着日本要求上海所有中国广播电台向哈同大楼（Hardoon Building）内的广播电台监理处登记的截止日期于今日到来，上海公共租界工部局今天下午在行政大厦召开会议。在此次会议上，董事们将听取主席 C. S. Franklin 先生关于

位于爱文义路（Avenue Road）、被称为海外广播公司（Overseas Broadcasting Company）的 XMHC 电台，昨日收到一份 dated 5月3日、由广播监理处处长 K. Asano 少校签署的通知，命令其停止营业。XMHC 的业主为拥有美国国籍的中国人，并声明其电台已在美国领事馆注册为美资企业。命令写道：“鉴于未能遵守1938年3月28日第3号通告中 circulated 的建议，现严令贵台立即停止进一步广播。”

他近期与日本当局为解决这一棘手问题而进行的谈判结果或进展的报告。
然而，今日人们并不认为此事已达成任何明确协议。来自各方的报道不一，但似乎虽然尚未找到 accord，但如果要求未得到满足，日本人不太可能立即采取强制手段停止广播。
半数停播
在大约20家较大的中国广播电台中，有一半已经停止运营，而不愿服从日本的控制。在剩下的10家中，有一家是中国基督教机构，播放宗教内容。其余九家继续广播，但据悉只有一家持有日本许可证。大多数电台位于公共租界的西部。
今日在一些消息灵通的外国人士圈子里，人们相信已达成一项安排，即这些电台将在日本批准的条件下向工部局注册，其中当然包括规定必须从节目中删除反日内容。然而，在其他圈子里，人们认为达成此类协议的可能性极小。日本非官方消息来源表明，截至今天上午，尚未达成任何协议。

仍在广播
今日一份中文报告称，未注册的电台今日照常广播，并决心不向日本无线电监理处注册，并补充说这些电台宁愿停业。
大多数电台约在一周前停止工作，尽管有几家电台在几天后恢复了运营。当时日本人威胁说，除非服从其命令，否则他们将移除租界内中国电台的部分设备，以防止进一步广播。中国电台愿意提供所需信息，但不直接提供给日本人，而是倾向于与工部局打交道。大多数电台上周已将信息发送给工部局。
日本人任何试图从电台移除设备的举动可能会被视为严重事件，因为这些电台属于私有财产。据说外国业主正在尽一切努力避免任何可能因中国电台被迫关闭而产生的摩擦，因为这涉及到与之竞争的外国电台。

Cease To Broadcast

The deadlock between Chinese
broadcasting stations and the
Shanghai Broadcasting Station Sup-
ervising Bureau, which has asked
the former to register has
not yet been broken. Some
of the stations have now decided
to suspend their programmes in-
definitely. It is reported that the

ing stations have definitely decided

Chinese station, the Fu Ying Broad-
casting Station, however, has de-
cided to resume business to-day.
This station is a religious one in-
volving British and American in-
terests and its programmes are
religious in nature.

The Shanghai Municipal Council
has reportedly sent representatives
to negotiate with those in charge
of the supervising bureau, but no
satisfactory results have been ob-
tained.

It will be recalled that when the
bureau served notices to the
various broadcasting stations re-
quiring them to register, it was
clearly stated that unless the sta-

steps would be taken.

84

广播僵局
仍未打破

中国电台将
暂停广播

中国广播电台与要求前者注册的上海广播电台监理处之间的僵局尚未打破。一些电台现已决定无限期暂停节目。据报道，上海公共租界工部局将保护那些决定关闭的电台的财产。

据一份中文晚报报道，三家大型中国广播电台已明确决定关闭并拒绝注册。然而，一家名为福英广播电台（Fu Ying Broadcasting Station）的中国电台决定于今日恢复营业。该电台是一家涉及英美利益的宗教电台，其节目性质为宗教内容。

据报道，上海公共租界工部局已派代表与监理处负责人进行谈判，但未获得满意结果。

回想起来，当监理处向各广播电台发出通知要求其注册时，曾明确声明，除非电台注册，否则将采取适当措施。

暂无新闻广播
目前
由于不可控的情况，《字林西报》（North-China Daily News）将通过 XMHD 电台进行的新闻广播暂停，直至另行通知。一旦新闻广播恢复，将立即告知听众。

pages.en:
Chinese
Stations
Protest

Broadcasting Said Not
Possible; Council
Negotiating

There continued to be an unfamiliar quiet in the Shanghai other yesterday as Chinese broadcasting stations remained closed. Efforts were being made to clear up the misunderstanding in connection with the recent request issued by the newly organized Broadcasting Supervising Service.

The Chinese station owners were said to be dealing with the bureau through the Shanghai Municipal Council. The Council, it was stated, had been furnished with necessary information on the several radio stations involved.

Foreign stations and two new stations sponsored by the Japanese continued to operate yesterday. The programmes featured by the latter included Peking girls singing Chinese songs and playing melodies on native violins.

Businessmen here claimed that they were suffering a loss because their advertising schedules on local stations had been disrupted. It was the station owners, however, who were suffering most and hoping for an early solution of the question.
pages.zh:
中国
电台
抗议

称无法广播；
工部局正在
谈判

昨日，随着中国广播电台继续关闭，上海呈现出一种异样的寂静。人们正努力澄清与新成立的广播监理处最近发出的请求有关的误解。

据说中国电台业主正通过上海公共租界工部局与该局打交道。据悉，工部局已获提供有关涉及的几家广播电台的必要信息。

外国电台和两家由日本赞助的新电台昨日继续运营。后者的节目特色包括北京女孩演唱中国歌曲并用民族小提琴演奏旋律。

这里的商人声称，由于在当地电台的广告安排被打乱，他们遭受了损失。然而，遭受损失最大并希望早日解决这一问题的是电台业主。

pages.en:
14 Broadcast
Stations Still
Not Operating

Off Air Because Of
Squabble Over
Censorship

INFORMATION IS
GIVEN TO S.M.C

Oppose Japanese Plan
For Regulation
Of Ether

Some 14 local Chinese-owned radio stations are likely to remain off the air for the second day today as a result of the impasse arising out of the refusal of the broadcasters to comply with the new Japanese regulations for registration.

The 14 stations involved in the present squabble voluntarily suspended operations yesterday morning, which was the deadline set by the Nipponese authorities for all registration procedure to be completed.

S.M.C. Negotiates

Officials of the Shanghai Municipal Council were yesterday using their good offices in an attempt to iron out the difficulties. Up to late yesterday afternoon, however, they had not heard definitely from the Japanese authorities regarding the final disposal of the question.

Owners of the broadcasting stations who elected not to comply with the Japanese registration procedure have on their own accord supplied all the information desired by the Nipponese to the Council.

A plan whereby the Council will exercise the desired control over the stations in the Settlement is understood to have been placed before the Japanese authorities as a compromise arrangement for solving the impasse.

Eight Comply

Among some 20 Chinese-owned stations here some eight are understood to have complied with the Japanese regulation. Some of these stations continued to operate yesterday.

The present trouble was foreshadowed at the end of last month when the "Broadcasting Superintendence Office," with offices at Room 316 Hardoon Building, announced its formation. On April 8 a notification bearing the chop of the organization was circulated among all local stations, stating that the broadcasters would not be allowed to operate unless they register with the control organization by April 15.

At that time, the majority of the local station owners hesitated to comply with the request. In the first place, it was stated, the control office failed to make public any form of regulation regarding its supervision of radio broadcasting. This failure, the station owners pointed out, makes it impossible for them to recognize the extent of controlling power of the new office.

Permit Involved

At the same time, the circular of the control office also asked station owners to produce the permits given to the stations by the Ministry of Communications of the National Government. As these certificates are difficult to secure and are the licenses permitting the stations to operate, it was feared that confiscation of these documents would seriously jeopardize the position of the broadcasters.

As a result of these difficulties, the majority of the station owners ignored the registration regulation. In the meantime, the control organization sent out another notice, postponing the final deadline to April 27. The postponement, however, failed to bring in any new applicants for registration, except a few small stations.

Stations Threatened

During the past several days, the various recalcitrant broadcasters were given to understand that unless they register promptly, their stations will be visited and important parts of their machines would be taken away so that their stations would be crippled.

As a result of this threat, police guards, it is understood, have been posted in the vicinity of the various stations.

With the approach of the deadline for registration, station owners held another meeting at which it was decided that the Council should be informed of their problem. It was felt that the fact that the stations are located within the Settlement makes the question revolve around the issue of the Council's administrative rights.

Following the request of the broadcasters, the Council took up the question with the Japanese authorities. Meantime, the information desired by the Japanese control authorities was supplied by the various stations to the Settlement police. This information includes:

1.—The name of the proprietor or group of owners, nationality, age, place of residence and other pertinent information.
2.—The purpose of the station's operation.
3.—The financial status of the station and the source of revenue.
4.—Power, location and detailed plans of the transmitting equipment.
5.—Location of the studio.
6.—Call signal.
7.—Frequency of the transmitter.
8.—Names of announcers and engineers, their nationality, age, place of residence and salary.
9.—A copy of the permit, if any, issued by the Ministry of Communications.

Local foreign-owned stations are not involved in the present issue, although they have received similar notifications as the Chinese broadcasters. The foreign stations paid no heed to the notice and the Japanese authorities have not pressed the issue, preferring apparently to deal with the Chinese stations first.

14 家广播电台
仍停止播音

因审查权之争
而停播

已向工部局
提供信息

反对日本管制
无线电波之计划

由于广播公司拒绝遵守新的日本登记规定，由此陷入僵局，约 14 家本地华人拥有的广播电台今天可能第二天继续停播。

卷入当前纠纷的这 14 家电台于昨天上午自愿停止运营，昨天是日本当局设定的完成所有登记手续的最后期限。

工部局进行斡旋

上海公共租界工部局官员昨日从中斡旋，试图消除困难。然而，截至昨日下午晚些时候，他们尚未从日本当局那里得到关于该问题最终处置的确切消息。

选择不遵守日本登记程序的广播电台业主已主动向日方提供了工部局所要求的所有信息。

据悉，一项由工部局对租界内电台行使所需管控权的计划，已作为解决僵局的妥协方案提交给日本当局。

八家电台遵从

在此地约 20 家华人拥有的电台中，据悉有八家已遵守日本规定。其中一些电台昨天继续运营。

目前的麻烦在上月底已现端倪，当时设在哈同大楼（Hardoon Building）316 室的“广播监理处”宣布成立。4 月 8 日，该机构盖印的通知在本地所有电台间分发，声明除非广播公司在 4 月 15 日前向该管控机构登记，否则不得运营。

当时，大多数本地电台业主犹豫是否遵从此项要求。首先，据称，该监理处未公布任何关于其监管无线电广播的规章形式。电台业主指出，这种缺失使他们无法确认新机构的管控权力范围。

涉及许可证

同时，该监理处的通函还要求电台业主出示国民政府交通部颁发给电台的许可证。由于这些证书难以获取，且是允许电台运营的执照，人们担心没收这些文件将严重危及广播公司的地位。

由于这些困难，大多数电台业主无视了登记规定。与此同时，该管控机构发出另一份通知，将最后期限推迟至 4 月 27 日。然而，除了几家小电台外，这次延期并未带来任何新的登记申请者。

电台受到威胁

在过去几天里，各家不服从的广播公司被告知，除非他们迅速登记，否则其电台将遭到搜查，机器的重要部件将被带走，致使电台瘫痪。

据悉，由于这一威胁，警察警卫已被部署在各电台附近。

随着登记截止日期的临近，电台业主举行了另一次会议，决定将其问题告知工部局。人们认为，鉴于电台位于租界内，这一问题围绕着工部局行政权的问题展开。

应广播公司的请求，工部局与日本当局交涉了此事。同时，各电台已向租界警务处提供了日本管控当局所需的信息。这些信息包括：

1.—业主或业主团体的姓名、国籍、年龄、居住地及其他相关信息。
2.—电台运营的目的。
3.—电台的财务状况及收入来源。
4.—发射设备的功率、位置及详细图纸。
5.—演播室的位置。
6.—呼号。
7.—发射频率。
8.—播音员和工程师的姓名、国籍、年龄、居住地及薪水。
9.—如有，交通部颁发的许可证副本。

本地外资拥有的电台不涉及当前问题，尽管它们收到了与华人广播公司类似的通知。外国电台未理会该通知，日本当局也未紧逼此事，显然更倾向于先处理华人电台。

（批注：归档）

Shanghai's Radio Crisis
VOLUNTARY CLOSING-DOWN of most of the Chinese radio stations in Shanghai has resulted from Japanese efforts to assume control over them. It is the position of the stations that they are willing to furnish required information to the foreign area authorities but not to any "broadcasting bureau" set up by the Japanese, and they would rather go off the air (at least for the time being) than comply.

The issues involved are tangled, as with much else in Shanghai today. Looking back, we see the present picture reversed a few years ago when the National Government sought to control broadcasting with reference both to Chinese and foreign stations. To trace through the history of the matter briefly may shed some light on the present set-up.

At the time Nanking sought to step into the radio picture, matters in Shanghai were completely chaotic with every station doing as it pleased so long as it did not embroil itself with Settlement or Concession authorities as might have been the case had it, for example, sought to put too-ribald songs or matter annoying some foreign national officialdom on the air. "Jimmy" James had just conducted a contest to choose a call-letter name for his station and some ingenious wight had won by suggesting RUOK—Are You O.K.? In such a state of freedom the foreign stations in particular were extremely reluctant at first to admit that anybody save the foreign authorities in Shanghai had any right of control.

But in this position they speedily found themselves out on a long limb. International agreement on the point was clear. Sovereignty over the ether waves resided in the sovereign Power, China, just as truly in the Settlement and Concession as in Chapei or Nantao. And even the stations agreed that for their own interest it was desirable that there be some single authority able to govern such matters as wave-length allocations to prevent jamming. The foreign authorities kept their measure of control by accompanying the Chinese officials and attending to such enforcement measures as were desired by the radio broadcasting department of the Ministry of Communications. In accordance with international practice, uniform call-letters (in this case all beginning with "X" which was just Mr. James' hard luck) were adopted.

The present position is one where the Chinese stations are targets, not the foreign. But it is hard to see how any principle can differentiate between the two when it is applied within the foreign areas, where after all Japan is not yet top dog though Japan admittedly utters a lusty bark. If the issue is to be purely one of principle, anything applying to Chinese stations would have to apply to foreign stations just as the contrary rule was administered previously.

It can hardly be admitted that the Japanese have inherited the Chinese Government's rights in this respect. Japan is not sovereign Power; neither Japan nor Japan's puppets are recognized by the foreign nations, while on the other hand the National Government continues to be recognized.

A threat has been made that if the Chinese stations did not comply with the Japanese demand, their property would be entered and vital operating mechanism would be removed. Probably it was this threat which has caused voluntary shutting-down of most of the stations, since it admittedly would be most embarrassing to the foreign authorities to have such an issue come to an acute stage. The Japanese have done such things previously, in other cases (involving Chinese newspapers) they have threatened to act if the foreign authorities did not, and they still hold control of north-of-the-Creek areas by force majeure if anyone were interested in that point as a precedent.

Our guess is that the Japanese claims to control will not be recognized, thus preserving foreign stations from a pressure which the Japanese do not in their case wish to exercise anyway; but that as a matter of practical expediency the foreign area authorities will see to it that Japanese wishes are in general respected with reference to operation of Chinese stations.

With this the "Broadcasting Superintendent's Office" operated by the Japanese in the Hardoon Building should, and probably will, be satisfied. Its legal claim to control broadcasting cannot possibly stand up. But the Settlement and Concession authorities themselves have the right and even obligation to see to it that broadcasting within foreign areas is not of a nature unduly to ruffle the susceptibilities of anyone, including the Japanese—and the Chinese too, if it comes to that.

上海的无线电危机

上海大多数华人广播电台的自愿关闭，源于日本试图接管控制这些电台的努力。电台方面的立场是，他们愿意向外国区域当局提供所需信息，但不愿向日本设立的任何“广播局”提供，他们宁愿停播（至少暂时如此），也不愿顺从。

所涉及的问题错综复杂，正如当今上海的许多其他事情一样。回顾过去，我们看到几年前的情形与现在截然相反，当时国民政府试图控制广播，涉及华人和外国电台。简要追溯此事的历史，或许能阐明当前的局面。

当南京方面试图介入无线电领域时，上海的情况完全混乱，每家电台都随心所欲，只要不卷入租界或公董局当局即可——例如，如果电台播放过于淫秽的歌曲或令某些外国官员恼火的内容，就可能会卷入当局。当时，“吉米”·詹姆斯（"Jimmy" James）刚刚为其电台举办了一场征集呼号的比赛，一位聪明人凭借建议“RUOK”（Are You O.K.?/你还好吗？）获胜。在这种自由状态下，外国电台起初极不情愿承认除上海外国当局以外的任何人拥有管控权。

但在这种立场上，他们很快发现自己陷入了孤立无援的境地。在这一问题上的国际协定是明确的。无线电波的主权属于主权国家中国，这在租界和公董局辖区与在闸北或南市一样真实。甚至电台也同意，出于自身利益，最好有一个单一的权威机构来管理波长分配等事务，以防止干扰。外国当局通过陪同中国官员并处理交通部无线电广播部门所需的执法措施，保持了其一定程度的控制权。按照国际惯例，采用了统一的呼号（在这种情况下，所有呼号均以“X”开头，这对詹姆斯先生来说真是运气不佳）。

目前的局势是，华人电台成为目标，而非外国电台。但是，很难看出当这一原则应用于外国区域时，如何区分两者，毕竟日本在那里尚未占据主导地位，尽管日本确实发出了强有力的叫嚣。如果这纯粹是一个原则问题，那么适用于华人电台的任何规定也必须适用于外国电台，正如以前执行相反规则时那样。

很难承认日本在此方面继承了中国政府的权利。日本不是主权国家；日本及其傀儡政权均未得到外国承认，而另一方面，国民政府继续得到承认。

有人威胁称，如果华人电台不遵守日本的要求，其财产将被闯入，关键的操作机制将被移除。很可能正是这一威胁导致了大多数电台的自愿关闭，因为诚然，如果此类问题发展到尖锐阶段，将使外国当局极为尴尬。日本人以前在其他案例（涉及中文报纸）中也做过此类事情，他们威胁说如果外国当局不行动，他们就会行动，而且如果有人关心这一点作为先例的话，他们仍然通过不可抗力控制着苏州河以北地区。

我们的猜测是，日本的管控主张将不被承认，从而使外国电台免受日本在其情况下本就不愿施加的压力；但出于实际权宜之计，外国区域当局将确保在与华人电台运营相关的事项上，日本的愿望大体上得到尊重。

如此一来，日本在哈同大楼运营的“广播监理处”应该，并且可能会感到满意。其管控广播的法律主张根本站不住脚。但是，租界和公董局当局本身有权甚至有义务确保外国区域内的广播性质不会过度激怒任何人，包括日本人——如果必要的话，也包括中国人。

May 6, 1938.
Morning Translation

Standard and other local newspapers :-

THE REGISTRATION OF RADIO BROADCASTING STATIONS

On April 28 local Chinese commercial radio broadcasting stations voluntarily suspended their business over the question of registration. At the request of commercial and charitable bodies, a few of the broadcasting stations subsequently resumed operations, but the question of registration still remains unsettled. The Japanese authorities are watching the situation closely.

It is learned that Asano, Chief of the Radio Broadcasting Stations Control Office, called on Mr. Franklin, Chairman of the S.M.C., and Mr. Fessenden, Secretary-General, the other day, but no agreement was reached. He then decided to take drastic action as from May 4.

At noon May 4, twelve radio broadcasting stations located within the International Settlement, namely the Lee Lee (利利), the Tung Fang (東方), the Fuh Ying (佛音), the Yu Lien (友聯), the Tung Loh (東陸), the Sun Sun (新新), the Foh Ying (福音), the Lah Yah (大亞), the Hwa Mei (華美), the Overseas (華僑), the Jimmy's (奇美) and the French Club (法總會), which had not registered, received a fourth notice from the Radio Broadcasting Stations Control Office stating that they would be prohibited from carrying on their business if they persisted in refusing to register.

Of the three broadcasting stations in the French Concession, the Yuen Chong Broadcasting Station (元昌電台) was ordered to suspend business on April 20 by the French authorities at the instance of the Japanese for having broadcasted an anti-Japanese programme, while the Foo Sing (富星) and the Dah Ching Hwa (大中華) are still closed.

According to the Radio Broadcasting Stations Control Office, all stations will hereafter be required to register and to submit to supervision.

A new station known as the Dah Kwong Ming (大光明) Broadcasting Station began to function at noon yesterday.

Ta Mei Pao :-

Broadcasting May Be Resumed May 10

According to information received, the Japanese have agreed to the principle that Chinese broadcasting stations need not register with them but should submit to strict supervision by the S.M.C. and will cease to broadcast anti-Japanese programmes.

Yesterday the Radio Broadcasting Station Owners' Association held a meeting at which it was decided that all stations be immediately restored to the situation existing prior to April 23. It is probable that all the stations will be fully restored by May 10.

These stations which have resumed business have not registered with the Japanese and have, for business reasons, continued their service in accordance with the stipulations laid down by the S.M.C.

1938年5月6日。
晨间译件

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：-

广播电台登记事宜

4月28日，本地华商广播电台因登记问题自愿停业。应商业及慈善团体的请求，少数电台随后恢复运营，但登记问题仍未解决。日本当局正密切关注事态发展。

据悉，广播电台管制所所长浅野（Asano，音译）日前拜会了工部局总董富兰克林先生（Mr. Franklin）及总办费森登先生（Mr. Fessenden），但未达成协议。他随即决定自5月4日起采取严厉行动。

5月4日中午，位于公共租界内且未登记的十二家广播电台，即利利电台、东方电台、佛音电台、友联电台、东陆电台、新新电台、福音电台、大亚电台、华美电台、华侨电台、奇美电台及法总会电台，收到广播电台管制所发出的第四号通知，称若其坚持拒绝登记，将被禁止营业。

在法租界的三家电台中，元昌电台因播放反日节目，应日本方面要求，于4月20日被法国当局责令停业；而富星电台和大中华电台目前仍处于关闭状态。

据广播电台管制所称，今后所有电台均须登记并接受监管。

一家名为大光明电台的新电台于昨日中午开始播音。

《大美晚报》：-

广播可能于5月10日恢复

据收到的消息，日本人已同意一项原则，即中国广播电台无需向其登记，但须接受工部局的严格监管，并将停止播放反日节目。

昨日，广播电台业主协会召开会议，决定将所有电台立即恢复至4月23日之前的状况。预计所有电台将于5月10日前完全恢复。

这些已恢复营业的电台并未向日本人登记，而是出于商业原因，按照工部局的规定继续提供服务。

May 5, 1938.                                      Morning Translation.

Life Daily News and other local newspapers :-

JAPANESE AND THE BROADCASTING STATIONS

Some time ago the Japanese authorities formed
a Radio Broadcasting Station Control Office and ordered all
stations to register before April 27. On April 28 the
Chinese broadcasting stations suspended operations. For
the sake of peace and order, the Shanghai Municipal Council
mediated but without result.
The situation now stands as follows :-
(1) The following nine stations: the Tung Fung
(東方), Tung Loh (東陸), Yau Lien (友聯), Yuan Chong (元昌),
Ta Chung Hwa (大中華), Fu Shing (富星), Great China
Dispensary (中藥房), Ta Loh (大陸) and Hwa Tung (華東)
have decided to suspend operations indefinitely.
(2) The Fu Ying (福音) Broadcasting Station,
which is established by foreign and Chinese Christians,
are continuing to broadcast on the advice of the British
and American Consulates.
(3) The Li Shu Tun Dong (李樹屯堂) Station had
never suspended its broadcasting, while the Hong Nyieh (宏業),
Hwa Tai (華泰), Hwa Shing (華興), Kuo Hwa (國華), Ming
Yuen (明園), Chien Hwa (建華), Ta Mei (大美) and Ta Ya
(大亞) stations have resumed operations.
Yesterday the Broadcasting Station Control
Office issued a fourth order to the broadcasting stations
stating that all stations that had not registered must
cease broadcasting immediately. It is said that the
Chinese stations are prepared to suspend broadcasting en bloc.
The report in yesterday's papers that the Hwa
Tung Station had resumed operations is incorrect.

1938年5月5日。 晨间译件。

《生活日报》及其他本地报纸：-

日本人与广播电台

前些时候，日本当局成立了一个广播电台管制所，命令所有电台在4月27日前登记。4月28日，中国广播电台停止运营。为了和平与秩序，上海公共租界工部局进行了调解，但无果而终。
目前局势如下：-
(1) 以下九家电台：东方电台、东陆电台、友联电台、元昌电台、大中华电台、富星电台、中药房电台、大陆电台和华东电台，已决定无限期停止运营。
(2) 由中外基督徒创办的福音电台，在英国和美国领事馆的建议下，继续播音。
(3) 李树屯堂（Li Shu Tun Dong，音译）电台从未停止播音，而宏业电台、华泰电台、华兴电台、国华电台、明园电台、建华电台、大美电台和大亚电台已恢复运营。
昨日，广播电台管制所向各广播电台发出第四号命令，称所有未登记的电台必须立即停止播音。据说，中国电台准备集体停播。
昨日报纸上关于华东电台已恢复运营的报道是不实的。

May 5, 1938. Afternoon Translation

Standard publishes the following article :-

APPEAL TO LOCAL RADIO BROADCASTING STATIONS

The attempt of the Japanese to control the Chinese commercial radio broadcasting stations is reaching a critical stage; there is no ground for compromise because a compromise means surrender. On the surface, the radio broadcasting business has no political significance, but it may be compelled to disseminate groundless reports or absurd speeches, to do any of which is an act of treachery. At this time of crisis, every proprietor of a radio broadcasting station should refuse to register even at the cost of closing his business.

It is with deep regret, however, that this point has not been noted by a number of short-sighted persons whose action is helping the aggressors. It is learned that of these persons who are thus actively engaged are one Li (李 a relative of Mayoral Li Mao-jih 李茂之), the owner of a radio broadcasting station, one Hsu (許), a sectional chief of a certain radio broadcasting station, one Ching (景), an advertisement canvasser, one Huang (黃), manager of a certain phonograph records company and several others.

We must closely watch the developments in this affair. We learn that the Ministry of Communications of the National Government has detailed officials to make an investigation.

Members of the radio broadcasting enterprises,-
As you are a Chinese, do you want to conduct propaganda on behalf of the Japanese?
pages.zh:
1938年5月5日。午后译件

《字林西报》刊登以下文章：-

致本地广播电台的呼吁

日本人试图控制中国商业广播电台的行动正达到关键阶段；没有妥协的余地，因为妥协意味着投降。表面上看，无线电广播业务没有政治意义，但它可能被迫传播毫无根据的报道或荒谬的言论，做任何这样的事都是叛国行为。在这个危机时刻，每一位广播电台业主都应拒绝登记，即使以关闭业务为代价。

然而，令人深感遗憾的是，这一观点未被一些短视之人所注意，他们的行动正在帮助侵略者。据悉，积极参与此事的人中包括一名李姓人士（李，系市长李茂之的亲属），其为一家广播电台的业主；一名许姓人士，为某广播电台的科长；一名景姓人士，为广告招揽员；一名黄姓人士，为某唱片公司经理，以及其他几人。

我们必须密切关注此事的发展。我们获悉，国民政府交通部已派遣官员进行调查。

广播业同仁们，-
身为中国人，你们愿意替日本人做宣传吗？

pages.en:
May 4, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

Hwa Mei Chen Pao:

JAPANESE AND THE BROADCASTING STATIONS

As a protest against the Japanese attempt
to force them to register, the local radio broadcasting
stations suspended operations. Although no settlement
has yet been reached, the various stations have resumed
broadcasting one after another and yesterday programmes
were broadcasted by the Hwa Tung (華東), the Hwa Shing
(華興), the Kuo Hwa (國華), the Hong Nyieh (航業), the
Ta Mei (大美), the Chien Hwa (建華), the Ming Yuen
(明園), the Li Shu Tuk Dong (李樹德堂), the Tung Loh
(大陸), the Sun Sun (新新) and the Ta Ya (大亞)
Stations as well as the foreign owned stations.
The radio stations state that they have
resumed broadcasting at the request of various shops.
They refuse to discuss the question of registration.
According to the S.M.C., it has not yet
adopted the suggestion that the Council conduct this
registration.
Owing to certain difficulties, the Great
China (中華), the Ta Loh (大陸) and the Tung Fong
(東方) Stations will suspend operations permanently,
while the Yuen Chong (元昌), the Fu Sin (富星), the Ta
Chung Hwa (大中華) and the Yu Lien (友聯) Stations in the
French Concession have voluntarily ceased operations and
dismantled their plant.
pages.zh:
1938年5月4日。午后译件。

《华美晨报》：

日本人与广播电台

为抗议日本人强迫其登记，本地广播电台停止了运营。虽然尚未达成解决方案，但各家电台已陆续恢复播音，昨日华东电台、华兴电台、国华电台、航业电台、大美电台、建华电台、明园电台、李树德堂电台、大陆电台、新新电台和大亚电台以及外商拥有的电台均播放了节目。
电台方面表示，他们是应各家商号的要求恢复播音的。他们拒绝讨论登记问题。
据工部局称，其尚未采纳由工部局进行此项登记的建议。
由于某些困难，中华电台、大陆电台和东方电台将永久停止运营，而位于法租界的元昌电台、富星电台、大中华电台和友联电台已自愿停止运营并拆除了设备。

pages.en:
May 3, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

Standard and other local newspapers :-

JAPANESE AND THE RADIO BROADCASTING STATIONS

The question of registration of local commercial radio broadcasting stations is still unsettled despite the negotiations between the Shanghai Municipal Council and the Radio Broadcasting Station Control Office established by the Japanese authorities. The latter is insisting that the stations should comply with regulations.
According to information secured by our reporter, a number of local radio broadcasting stations, with the exception of the Great China Dispensary Broadcasting Station (中西電台), the Dah Loh Broadcasting Station (大陸電台), the Tung Fang Broadcasting Station (東方電台) and some others, have decided to suspend operations. The S.M.C. has decided to give every protection to those stations which have suspended operations because, according to the opinion of various circles, the buildings and machinery of radio stations will become private property once they close down and that it is the duty of the S.M.C. to protect property belonging to residents of the Settlement.
pages.zh:
1938年5月3日。午后译件。

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：-

日本人与广播电台

尽管上海公共租界工部局与日本当局设立的广播电台管制所进行了谈判，但本地商业广播电台的登记问题仍未解决。后者坚持要求电台遵守规定。
据本报记者获得的消息，除中西电台、大陆电台、东方电台及其他几家电台外，多数本地广播电台已决定停止运营。工部局决定对已停业的电台给予充分保护，因为各界认为，广播电台一旦关闭，其建筑和机器将成为私有财产，而保护属于租界居民的财产是工部局的职责。

pages.en:
May 2, 1938. Morning Translation.

Morning Leader and other local newspapers :-

JAPANESE AND THE BROADCASTING STATIONS

The local Chinese radio broadcasting stations
have suspended operations for four days already. The
Shanghai Municipal Council has suggested a compromise,
but this was rejected by the Japanese authorities on the
ground that the matter was in the hands of the Ministries
of War, Navy and Foreign Affairs of the Japanese Government.
Most of the Chinese stations are determined not
to resume broadcasting unless a satisfactory settlement
is reached. After the affair came to a deadlock on the
evening of April 30, some of the stations began to dismantle
their machinery.
The Li Shu Tuh Dong (李樹德堂), the Hong Kyish
(獻業), the Ta Ya (大亞) and the Ta Mei (大美) Stations,
however, continued to broadcast. The Kuo Hwa (國華),
Hwa Shing (華興) and Ming Yuen (明遠) Stations resumed
broadcasting on the morning of May 1. (According to one
report, the resumption was due to certain circumstances.)
Another station, the Hwa Tai (華泰), resumed broadcasting
in the evening.
The stations that have suspended operations will
issue a manifesto dealing with those that have resumed
operations.
pages.zh:
1938年5月2日。晨间译件。

《晨报》及其他本地报纸：-

日本人与广播电台

本地中国广播电台已停业四天。上海公共租界工部局曾建议妥协，但被日本当局以该事项掌握在日本政府陆军省、海军省和外务省手中为由予以拒绝。
大多数中国电台决心在未达成满意解决方案之前不恢复播音。4月30日晚此事陷入僵局后，部分电台开始拆除机器。
然而，李树德堂电台、献业电台、大亚电台和大美电台继续播音。国华电台、华兴电台和明远电台于5月1日上午恢复播音。（据一则报道，恢复播音是由于某些情况所致。）
另一家电台，华泰电台，于晚间恢复播音。
已停业的电台将发表一份宣言，涉及那些已恢复运营的电台。

pages.en:
May 1, 1938.
Morning Translation.

Hua Mei Chen Pao and other local newspapers :-
THE LOCAL BROADCASTING STATIONS

No news is available as to when the
local Chinese radio broadcasting stations, which have
suspended operations because they refuse to register with
the Japanese authorities, will resume their services. The
authorities of the Foreign Settlements are paying close
attention to this matter and have already opened
negotiations with the Japanese authorities. The foreign
and Japanese radio stations are operating as usual.
It is said that through the mediation
of the authorities of the Foreign Settlements, the local
broadcasting stations will probably resume operations on
Monday next.
pages.zh:
1938年5月1日。
晨间译件。

《华美晨报》及其他本地报纸：-
本地广播电台

关于因拒绝向日本当局登记而停业的本地中国广播电台何时恢复服务，暂无消息。外国租界当局正密切关注此事，并已与日本当局展开谈判。外籍和日本广播电台照常运营。
据说，经外国租界当局调解，本地广播电台可能将于下周一恢复运营。

pages.en:
April 30, 1938. Morning Translation.

Morning Leader and other local newspapers :-

BROADCASTING STATIONS CEASING OPERATIONS

A tense situation prevails among local Chinese
broadcasting stations. The step taken by the stations has
the sympathy of the whole country.
All the Chinese broadcasting stations suspended
operations on April 28 with the exception of the Great China
Dispensary Broadcasting Station (中華), the Li Shu Tuh Dong
Broadcasting Station (李樹德堂), the Hong Nyieh Station
(航業), the Ta Ya Station (大亞) and the Ta Mei Station
(大美), the last two being established after the outbreak
of hostilities and are not licensed by the Chinese Government.
Of these five stations, the Ta Ya went off the
air after broadcasting for a few hours yesterday. The
Great China Dispensary Station ceased operations at 1.40
p.m. yesterday ostensibly to effect repairs to the machines,
but in reality its action was due to an incident that
occurred in the morning: during a programme which consists
of the broadcasting of orders sent over the telephone by
customers to the Great China Dispensary, a certain patriotic
person rang up the dispensary and shouted the slogan "Down
with the Japanese Imperialists".
As the Ta Mei Station yesterday was broadcasting
a special programme by Siao Vung-ping (筱文濱), a Shanghai
native play actor, who recently made a cinema film entitled
"The Dutiful Daughter-in-law" (賢慧媳婦), the station
received a warning from a patriotic person. Some person also
rang up the station and kept the line connected so that
people wishing to book tickets for the film were unable to
do so. The station later stopped its broadcasting.
The Hong Nyieh Station has declared that it
would continue broadcasting because it has nothing to do with
politics, but it also ceased operations yesterday.
The Li Shu Tuh Dong Station is now the only
Chinese station continuing to broadcast, without any
regard for the prestige of the country.
Despite the efforts of interested parties to
bring about a settlement, no agreement was reached. The
stations which have suspended operations have expressed their
determination not to resume broadcasting under conditions
detrimental to the sovereignty of the nation.
Up to yesterday morning, between 10 to 20 stations
had forwarded certain forms to the Shanghai Municipal Council
as a mark of their willingness to submit to control by the
Council. The S.M.C. has detailed police officers to all the
stations in the International Settlement to accord protection.
The cessation of broadcasting is seriously affecting
commercial circles.
pages.zh:
1938年4月30日。晨间译稿。

《晨报》及其他本地报纸：

广播电台停止运营

本地中文广播电台局势紧张。各电台所采取之举措，获得全国同情。
除中华大药房广播电台（中華）、李树德堂广播电台（李樹德堂）、航业电台（航業）、大亚电台（大亞）和大美电台（大美）外，所有中文广播电台均于4月28日停止运营，其中后两家系在战事爆发后设立，未获中国政府许可。
在这五家电台中，大亚电台昨日播出数小时后即停播。中华大药房电台于昨日下午1时40分停止运营，表面上声称是为了修理机器，但实际上其行动是由于上午发生的一起事件：在该电台播放顾客通过电话向中华大药房下达订单的节目期间，某位爱国人士致电药房，高呼“打倒日本帝国主义”的口号。
由于大美电台昨日正在播出上海本土滑稽戏演员筱文濱（Siao Vung-ping）的特别节目，该演员近期拍摄了一部名为《贤慧媳妇》的电影，电台收到了一位爱国人士的警告。还有人致电电台并一直占用线路，致使希望预订电影票的人无法办理。该电台随后停止了广播。
航业电台曾声明将继续广播，因其与政治无关，但昨日也停止了运营。
李树德堂电台是目前唯一继续广播的中文电台，全然不顾国家声誉。
尽管有关各方努力促成和解，但未达成协议。已停止运营的电台表示决心不在损害国家主权的条件下恢复广播。
截至昨日上午，约有10至20家电台已向上海工部局递交了某些表格，以示愿意接受工部局的管制。上海工部局已派遣警员前往公共租界内的所有电台提供保护。
广播停播正严重影响商界。

pages.en:
April 29, 1938. Morning Translation.

Warning Leader and other local newspapers :-

JAPANESE AND BROADCASTING STATIONS

Upon the withdrawal of Chinese troops from Shanghai, the radio broadcasting stations of the Shanghai City Government (K.C.900) and the Ministry of Communications (K.C.1200) as well as the Shanghai Broadcasting Station (上海) (K.C.1100) and the Hwa Mei Broadcasting Station (華美) (K.C.1060) ceased operations.
Later the Japanese authorities established a Greater Shanghai Broadcasting Station (大上海) which uses the same wave length and is supposed to be the successor to the broadcasting station of the former Shanghai City Government. The machines used by the Shanghai City Government Broadcasting Station were not taken over. Two well-known comedians named Liu Tsung-sai (劉春山) and Sung Ngai-ngai (盛呆呆) endeavoured to induce professional entertainers to broadcast at the new station but their efforts ended in failure.
Shortly before the end of March an Order No. 1, issued by the Radio Broadcasting Station Control Office, was received by foreign and Chinese broadcasting stations through the post stating that the Office would begin to censor broadcasting matters in the Hardoon Building as from April 1. The notice was ignored.
On about April 10 the broadcasting stations received Order No. 2 instructing them to register with the Control Office and apply for a permit before April 15.
On the evening of April 14 the French Police adopted protective measures at the broadcasting stations in the French Concession. Similar measures were later adopted by the authorities of the International Settlement. The broadcasting stations expressed their willingness to sacrifice themselves rather than injure the prestige of the country.
On April 28 Order No. 3 was received from the Japanese authorities extending the period of registration to April 27. The Yuen Chong (元昌), Fu Shing (富星) and Ta Chung Hwa (大中華) Broadcasting Stations in the French Concession then suspended operations. All the Chinese stations in the International Settlement suspended operations on the morning of April 28 with the exception of the Li Shu Tuh Dong Station (李書屠董), the Great China Dispensary Broadcasting Station (廣益), the Hang Hyleh Station (杭悅), the Ta Mei Station (大美) and the Ta Ya Station (大亞). Of these five stations, the last two mentioned are not approved by the Chinese Government and are not members of the Broadcasting Stations Association. The other three stations are reported to have registered with the Japanese authorities. It is also said that the Great China Dispensary Broadcasting Station and certain other stations have suggested to other stations that they comply with the registration through the Shanghai Municipal Council, but this is held by a number of stations to be unpatriotic. According to information received, the Ministry of Communications is investigating the matter.
Although the broadcasting stations in the French Concession have suspended operations, the French Police are not slackening their precautionary measures. In addition to stationing policemen at the broadcasting stations, armoured car patrols have been detailed to accord protection.
There are between twenty to thirty broadcasting stations in Shanghai.
pages.zh:
1938年4月29日。晨间译稿。

《警报报》及其他本地报纸：

日本人与广播电台

随着中国军队撤离上海，上海市政府（K.C.900）和交通部（K.C.1200）的无线电广播电台，以及上海广播电台（上海）（K.C.1100）和华美广播电台（華美）（K.C.1060）均停止运营。
随后，日本当局建立了一家大上海广播电台（大上海），使用相同的波长，据称是前任上海市政府广播电台的继承者。上海市政府广播电台所使用的机器并未被接管。两位名为刘春山（Liu Tsung-sai）和盛呆呆（Sung Ngai-ngai）的知名滑稽戏演员试图劝说职业艺人在新电台播音，但未能成功。
3月底前不久，外国及中文广播电台通过邮政收到无线电广播电台管制办公室发布的第1号命令，称该办公室将于4月1日起在哈同大楼（Hardoon Building）开始审查广播内容。该通知被无视。
4月10日左右，广播电台收到第2号命令，指示其在4月15日前向管制办公室登记并申请许可证。
4月14日晚，法国警察在法租界的广播电台采取了保护措施。随后，公共租界当局也采取了类似措施。各广播电台表示宁愿牺牲自己，也不愿损害国家声誉。
4月28日，收到日本当局发出的第3号命令，将登记期限延长至4月27日。法租界内的元昌（Yuen Chong）、富星（Fu Shing）和大中华（Ta Chung Hwa）广播电台随即停止运营。公共租界内的所有中文电台均于4月28日上午停止运营，例外的是李书屠董电台（李書屠董）、广益广播电台（廣益，即中华大药房）、杭悦电台（Hang Hyleh）、大美电台（大美）和大亚电台（大亞）。在这五家电台中，最后提到的两家未获中国政府批准，也不是广播电台协会的成员。据报道，其他三家电台已向日本当局登记。另有说法称，中华大药房广播电台及其他某些电台曾建议其他电台通过上海工部局进行登记，但这被许多电台视为不爱国行为。据收到的消息，交通部正在调查此事。
尽管法租界内的广播电台已停止运营，但法国警察并未放松警戒措施。除了在广播电台派驻警察外，还调派装甲车巡逻队提供保护。
上海约有二十至三十家电台。

pages.en:
A□□
May 28, 1938.
Afternoon Translation.

Standard :-

THE INTERNATIONAL RADIO STATION TO RESUME OPERATIONS

After it was taken over by the Japanese
authorities, the International Radio Station suspended
operations owing to lack of technical experts.
It is learned that through the efforts
of Ghui Ping (□), the President, and Chang Chao-peng
(张□鹏), a Sectional Chief, of the Radio Station, a
number of its former employees will return to work.
As Ghui Ping and Chang Chao-pang are
now about to help the Japanese instead of doing some service
for the country in this war of resistance, certain patriotic
employees of the Radio Station have petitioned the Ministry
of Communications to despatch officials to Shanghai to make
an investigation.
pages.zh:
A□□
1938年5月28日。
午后译稿。

《标准报》：

国际电台将恢复运营

国际电台被日本当局接管后，因缺乏技术专家而停止运营。
据悉，经该电台台长 Ghui Ping（□）和科长张□鹏（Chang Chao-peng）的努力，该电台部分前雇员将返回工作岗位。
由于 Ghui Ping 和张□鹏 如今即将协助日本人，而非在这场抗战中为国家效力，该电台某些爱国员工已请愿交通部派遣官员赴沪进行调查。

pages.en:
April 28, 1938. Morning Translation.

Morning Leader :-

JAPANESE TO CONTROL BROADCASTING

The Japanese recently organized a "Radio Broadcasting Station Control Office" and repeatedly issued orders instructing broadcasting stations in the French Concession and the International Settlement to register. The foreign-owned stations in the two Foreign Settlements have decided to ignore this order. The Chinese-owned stations were promised protection by the authorities of the Foreign Settlements and, with the exception of a few stations which ceased operations on April 20, they are continuing their broadcasting.
The broadcasting stations have now received another order, stating as follows:

"This office some time ago ordered all broadcasting stations to register before April 15. It is now notified that any station which fails to register with this office before April 27 will forfeit all privileges enjoyed by them.
Asamochi,
Chief of the Radio Broadcasting Station Control Office."

The Chinese-owned Fu Shing (富星) and Ta Chung Hwa (大中華) Broadcasting Stations, which are located in the French Concession and which are unwilling to submit to the control of the Japanese organization, will suspend operations as from to-day. The Chinese broadcasting stations in the International Settlement prefer to submit to the control of the Shanghai Municipal Council rather than to the Japanese authorities. They have asked the Council for advice and intend to call on the Council at 9 a.m. to-day to fill in certain forms.
pages.zh:
1938年4月28日。晨间译稿。

《晨报》：

日本人将管制广播

日本人最近组建了一个“无线电广播电台管制办公室”，并多次发布命令，指示法租界和公共租界内的广播电台进行登记。两个外侨居留地内的外商_owned_电台决定无视此命令。华商电台已获得外侨居留地当局的保护承诺，除少数几家于4月20日停止运营的电台外，其余均在继续广播。
各广播电台现已收到另一项命令，内容如下：

“本办公室此前命令所有广播电台于4月15日前登记。现通知如下：任何未在4月27日前向本办公室登记的电台，将丧失其享有的一切特权。
浅持（Asamochi），
无线电广播电台管制办公室主任。”

位于法租界、不愿服从日本机构管制的华商富星（富星）和大中华（大中華）广播电台，将从今日起停止运营。公共租界内的中文广播电台宁愿接受上海工部局的管制，也不愿受日本当局管辖。它们已向工部局寻求建议，并打算于今日上午9时拜访工部局，填写某些表格。
